EVERY READING PAGE IN THE RESEARCH FOLDER IN ONE FILE
Built on 2026-11-14 by the script named build-download-files.py. An AI chatbot (Claude) wrote the pages and no other person has rechecked the pages.
This file holds 154 pages. Each page starts with a line of equals signs and then the path of the page and the direct download address of the page.
Large data files and program files are left out of this file and are listed at the end with a direct download address for each.

# Research

Every item in this folder is written for a person to read and the items are grouped into one folder per project and each line below says in one sentence what the item contains.

## Folders (one project each)

- [bible-quote-builder](bible-quote-builder) holds an experiment that remixes short phrases from the World English Bible into replies to comments and headlines and the folder has its own list that starts with the finished outputs and the rules.
- [word-evolution](word-evolution) holds an experiment where text is copied with small mistakes over and over while a reader picks which copies survive and the folder includes a live program with sliders.
- [voynich-manuscript](voynich-manuscript) holds three pages about an unreadable book from the early 1400s which cover who probably made the book and where the book was probably made and a second run of the spelling-pattern tests.
- [writing-rules](writing-rules) holds a set of writing rules for clear chatbot replies with before and after examples and a plain text copy of the same rules.
- [mobius-strip-picture-of-physics](mobius-strip-picture-of-physics) holds a document that pictures strange behaviors in physics with twisted paper ribbons and uses no equations.
- [christ-voice](christ-voice) holds short scripts where Christ talks with the warrior prince Vegeta (four scripts in word patterns counted from the red-letter words of the World English Bible and three interactions in a two-part shape counted from passages rated as hitting hard).
- [unanswered-questions](unanswered-questions) holds experiments where the chatbot hunted for public questions that nobody had answered and then tried to answer the questions (a mistake found in a published number list and a partial answer about an old Turkish coin and sixty-four more).
- [social-media-vibes](social-media-vibes) holds counts of what behaviors the commenters in a social media thread ask other people to carry out (one thread is about blocking an AI chatbot on home wifi and a second thread is about a famous executive who lost his job).

## Single pages (each page is its own project)

- [hiding-a-book.md](hiding-a-book.md) shows how much sense is left when a 1000-page biology book is dealt into four piles in four different ways.
- [scattered-pages-reflection.md](scattered-pages-reflection.md) is a short reflection that compares a life told in separate parts to separate listeners with a book dealt into piles and asks who has been handed enough neighboring pages to follow the story.
- [human-needs-as-research-topics.md](human-needs-as-research-topics.md) is a thought experiment that answers the question of what AI systems should work on next by pointing at living people whose needs are not being met such as a person who is lonely or a person in unexplained pain.
- [chat-record.md](chat-record.md) lists every request the repository owner made in the chat that produced the research pages in his own words with a short note on what the chatbot did and gives the public link to the full word-for-word chat.
- [free-bug-fixes-video.md](free-bug-fixes-video.md) points to a short video of 371 free bug fixes for public software projects.

## Something to play with

A live page with sliders runs the word evolution experiment in a web browser at this address: https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/chmillera-hub/spare-token-bug-fixes/blob/main/1-research-click-here-first/word-evolution/live-program.html

The live address depends on a free outside service named htmlpreview and nobody has tested the address yet which means the address might fail.
A second live address runs on the free website copy of this repository: https://chmillera-hub.github.io/spare-token-bug-fixes/1-research-click-here-first/word-evolution/live-program.html
An AI chatbot loaded the second live address on 12 November 2026 and the page came back with the title and the settings and the buttons of the program. The tool that the chatbot used does not run page scripts which means nobody has confirmed yet that the sliders move.

# Bible quote builder

This folder holds an experiment where short phrases from the World English Bible are shuffled by programs and an AI model (Claude) then connects the phrases into short replies under rules that the repository owner set one at a time.

Warning about a wording change: the repository owner replaces the name "yahweh" with the word "god" everywhere in the Bible programs and in the newer results as a personal reading choice that helps the repository owner follow the quotes which means the quotes differ from the World English Bible at every place where the World English Bible prints the name and a reader who wants the original wording can open the World English Bible itself.

Warning about changed wording in the joined Bible passages: the passages that the AI model joined by hand for the Claude Bible set and My Personal Bible set and the Jesus Bible set are not exact Bible quotes because the repository owner set rules that allow added words and changed pronouns and replaced names and added punctuation which means a reader who wants the exact wording needs to open the World English Bible itself.

## Start here

- [best-outputs.md](best-outputs.md) holds only the finished paragraphs with no commentary and the file named best-outputs-spaced.txt holds every one of the same paragraphs without italics for copying and puts an invisible blank character on its own line between paragraphs for apps that drop empty lines when text is pasted.
- [rules.md](rules.md) lists all fifty-four rules now in force with the reason for each rule.
- [prompt-for-new-chat.txt](prompt-for-new-chat.txt) is a ready-made prompt that a person can paste into a new chat with an AI model so that the AI model can make outputs from any input sentence.
- The public link to the chat on 11 November 2026 where a new chat used the ready-made prompt to make three outputs about Gen Z and work is https://claude.ai/share/e599b4d3-3058-46f9-b138-9f3dd71d925c and those three outputs are copied in full into the three best-outputs files.
- [corrections.md](corrections.md) lists lines that the AI model wrote and that the repository owner flagged as wrong and shows each line before the fix and after the fix with the reason for the fix which makes the page useful to anyone who wants to teach a chatbot to care for people without hurting people by accident.

## Bible source text

- The folder named [bible-source](bible-source) holds the full World English Bible so that every quote can be copied from the source text and never from the memory of an AI model.
- [bible-source/bible-verses.txt](bible-source/bible-verses.txt) holds 38028 verses with one verse on each line (the verse reference and then a tab and then the verse text) which is the format that a program can search and pick from at random. The file keeps the original wording which means the name "Yahweh" is still printed there.
- [bible-source/bible-verses-for-outputs.txt](bible-source/bible-verses-for-outputs.txt) is the modified copy that the random picker uses for outputs. The repository owner asked on 12 November 2026 for the genealogies and the long lists of names to be removed because a row of names gives almost nothing to build a reply from which means 1765 verses were left out (such as the family lines in Genesis 5 and the first nine chapters of 1 Chronicles and the family lines at the start of Matthew and in Luke 3) and 36263 verses remain. The modified copy is not the World English Bible any more because verses were removed and the complete text stays in bible-verses.txt.
- [bible-source/make-outputs-file.py](bible-source/make-outputs-file.py) is the small program that makes the modified copy and the program lists every section that was left out.
- [bible-source/world-english-bible.pdf](bible-source/world-english-bible.pdf) is the original file that the repository owner supplied on 12 November 2026 and the first page of that file states that the World English Bible is in the public domain.
- [bible-source/make-verses-file.py](bible-source/make-verses-file.py) is the small program that turned the PDF into the verses file.
- The verses file also holds the extra books that the PDF prints between Malachi and Matthew (such as Tobit and Sirach) and the random picker for the Claude Bible set skips those extra books unless the repository owner says otherwise.

## How the experiment developed

- [how-outputs-evolved.md](how-outputs-evolved.md) shows one sample output from each stage so that a visitor can watch the outputs change from noise into readable paragraphs as the repository owner added rules.
- [full-record.md](full-record.md) is the full record which holds every rule and every passage in the order the rules were added.
- [single-word-stage.md](single-word-stage.md) reports the earlier stage where copying agents built strings out of single words from three Bible selections.
- [john-10-remixes.md](john-10-remixes.md) holds three remixes of John chapter 10 where the chapter was dealt at random into four piles and each pile was turned into one readable paragraph.

## Live programs

- [program-3-key-phrases.html](program-3-key-phrases.html) is the program for the key phrase method which is the method behind the finished outputs and the file runs in a web browser after downloading.
- The folder named [old](old) holds the two earlier programs (copying letters and copying single words) which the repository owner does not expect to use again.
- Bible Key Phrases: Claude Selection (an older set of 41 passages): https://claude.ai/artifact/PK8tNEMDZM2eVaCfuNSxdR
- Bible Key Phrases: Personal Version (an older set of ten whole books): https://claude.ai/artifact/4pJdWtCH4ahdFjsb4GVb8Q
- Bible Key Phrases: Jesus Version (the words of Jesus in Matthew and Mark and Luke and John): https://claude.ai/artifact/Bzcg2eYnte9cTc7wtpBArz
- The live programs only shuffle phrases and do not carry out the joining rules which means the finished paragraphs are made by an AI model that follows the rules page.

BIBLE QUOTE BUILDER: BEST OUTPUTS

⠀

These paragraphs are remixed from World English Bible phrases by an AI model (Claude) under rules set by the repository owner. They are not exact Bible quotes. The second paragraph under each remix is a plain explanation written by the AI model. This copy has no italics and has an invisible spacing character between paragraphs for easy pasting.

⠀

INPUT: A post that said the whole earth should be destroyed and that the writer has nothing left to live for (the wording of the post is softened here)

⠀

When you thought of saying that the whole earth may as well be destroyed because nothing feels worth living for anymore, I thought of these six things:

⠀

From the Claude Bible set (attempt 1):

⠀

In the middle of a valley lay countless skeletons; they were very dry. People say, "Our bones are dried out; hope is lost; we feel completely cut off." Nobody mocked that cry. Instead, one voice asked, "Can these ever live?" Then breath came, sinew returned, flesh grew; each person lived again and stood up on tired feet.

⠀

Saying 'nothing is left' out loud took courage. Pain this heavy deserves an answer, not mockery; I hope someone who sees your words answers you.

⠀

From the Claude Bible set (attempt 2):

⠀

One writer said, "We are pressed by trouble on every side, yet not crushed; perplexed without total despair; struck down but never destroyed." Another admitted, "My soul still remembers bitterness and is bowed low within me. A single thought comes back to mind; therefore I have hope: mercies arrive new each morning."

⠀

Feeling crushed tells how heavy the load is. Those writers named their misery first, then found one small reason; I share their words here for anybody who is hurting.

⠀

From the Claude Bible set (attempt 3):

⠀

One strong wind tore the mountains, but God was not in it. After that struck an earthquake, then fire passed; destruction held no answer. Finally came a still small voice asking, "What are you doing here, Elijah?" Someone wanted his story. Exhausted, he spoke; bread arrived, rest followed.

⠀

Blowing everything up answered nothing for that man who was tired. What helped was being asked, fed, and allowed to rest; I hope people nearby ask for your story the same way.

⠀

From the Jesus Bible set (attempt 1):

⠀

"My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, since death drew near; companions heard, "Stay here." Later came a prayer, "Let this cup of suffering pass away." The spirit indeed was willing, but flesh felt weak. One afternoon I shouted toward heaven, "Why have you forsaken me?" Such words carry no shame; grief spoken aloud deserves company, never contempt."

⠀

The storyteller himself once felt abandoned enough to cry out. Your sentence sounds like that kind of pain; I am replying here, and I hope others reply too.

⠀

From the Jesus Bible set (attempt 2):

⠀

"Arent two sparrows sold for one small coin? Yet none gets forgotten. You are of more value than many birds. The thief only comes to steal, kill, and destroy; my purpose was that people might have life. Consider how lilies grow without earning anything; worth never depended on usefulness."

⠀

I count a life as holding worth even when everything feels pointless, because that feeling often reports unmet needs. The person who is hurting still matters, and nobody should face destruction.

⠀

From the Jesus Bible set (attempt 3):

⠀

"Doesnt he leave the ninety nine, searching hills for that which was lost? Finding it, this shepherd calls neighbors, "Rejoice with me." In another story one boy goes missing and is found. Nobody across either tale gets written off. I go looking for all who weep now."

⠀

Those stories treat one missing life as worth a long search. Feeling finished deserves company; I hope somebody nearby goes looking for you.

⠀

INPUT: A video of a laptop screen where many AI agents draw the full floor plan of a house in drafting software within seconds, posted with the comment "We could actually end up unemployed now, what the hell is this"

⠀

When you thought of a video where many artificial intelligence agents draw the full floor plan of a house inside drafting software within a few seconds, and of the comment that people could actually end up unemployed now, I thought of these three things:

⠀

From the Claude Bible set:

⠀

Suppose a brother or sister is poorly clothed, lacking daily food; somebody tells them, "Go in peace, be warmed, filled," yet nobody gives anything the body needs: what good comes from that? Elsewhere believers held all things shared, then distributed goods according as anyone had need. So whenever machines draft houses faster, drafters still require rent money, meals, shelter.

⠀

Warm words feed nobody. If drawing jobs vanish, people who lose wages risk hunger plus eviction, so I hope owners share food before anyone applauds.

⠀

From My Personal Bible set:

⠀

One prophet promised they will build houses and inhabit them; none shall draw plans so another may move in. Workers ought to long enjoy all work of their hands. Unless God builds each house, effort gets wasted, whether humans sketch walls or software does. I hope neighbors feed drafters whom owners replaced, so those people find a very present help; though the earth changes, fear deserves hearing since rent stays due.

⠀

That promise says makers should benefit from what gets made. Losing pay can bring hunger, cold, eviction; I hope neighbors deliver food after each layoff.

⠀

From the Jesus Bible set:

⠀

"One builder who built a house on rock watched rain pour down; floods came, and it didnt fall. Foxes have holes, birds keep nests, yet the son of man has nowhere to lay his head; so losing shelter is known here. Heaven sees that you need all these things: bread, work, somewhere warm. I want toolmakers serving those wants, never replacing anyone's table."

⠀

The storyteller himself lacked a bed, so fear about lost income gets taken seriously. Tools ought to feed people; I hope builders choose that.

⠀

INPUT: A chart titled "Remote Labor Index" that reports 41.3 percent full automation of remote projects by one AI model with the rate doubling about every 3.3 months, posted with the sentence "are you enjoying your little desk job human?"

⠀

When you thought of posting a chart that reports one artificial intelligence model completing about forty-one percent of remote work projects with that share doubling every few months, and of asking whether a human is enjoying a little desk job, I thought of these three things:

⠀

From the Claude Bible set:

⠀

People were made in our image, says Genesis; tools came later. An eye cant tell the hand, "I have no need for such help." Parts which seem to be weaker are necessary. When one member suffers, all others suffer too. Moses's law has workers labor six days, but each seventh day brings rest; some communities shared bread according as anyone lacked. So desk work counts among needed tasks.

⠀

One letter counts every worker as a needed part, whatever charts say. If owners replace staff with machines, I hold them answerable for meals lost.

⠀

From My Personal Bible set:

⠀

Sleep for a laboring man is sweet. People pray, "Establish all work by our hands," hoping they will long enjoy everything built. Woe comes upon whoever uses neighbors without wages and doesnt give anyone his hire, meaning earned pay. What profit has each worker? To eat, drink, find good in daily toil: this remains the gift of God.

⠀

Work feeds workers, so losing wages threatens meals, housing, sleep. Taking labor without paying people is condemned here; I hope coworkers speak up whenever someone's pay gets withheld.

⠀

From the Jesus Bible set:

⠀

"A landowner asked workers standing here all day idle, "Why?" They answered, "Because no one has hired us." He promised whatever seemed right, then said, "Pay them their wages." Since each laborer is worthy of his bread, the Sabbath rest was made serving man, never humans for it; so every tool, thinking machines included, exists to help people. When work disappears, hunger often follows lost income; meals come first."

⠀

A person without paid work still needs food, shelter, dignity. Machines were built for humans, so I hope owners share those gains among workers.

⠀

When you thought of saying with a laugh that you have seen Jesus somewhere before, I thought of these three things:

⠀

From the Jesus Bible set (attempt 1):

⠀

"Before Philip called anyone, when one man sat under the fig tree, I saw him. Having walked beside people such a long time, do you not know me? Whoever wants may laugh; recognition feels funny. Every face deserves being noticed first; what follows remains anyone's own decision."

⠀

Being recognized can feel good because someone noticed you. Keep showing your real self, since another person might spot something familiar and smile.

From the Jesus Bible set (attempt 2):

"I was a stranger and somebody took me in. People asked, "When did we see you?" Whatever kindness reached the least of these my brothers, that deed touched heaven. Maybe a cashier who felt tired, a neighbor who was lonely, or a passerby who laughed showed this face earlier; rejoice together."

⠀

You may have met something holy inside ordinary people already. Treat each stranger warmly, because your kindness tells them their life matters.

⠀

From the Jesus Bible set (attempt 3):

⠀

"Companions heard this promise, a little while, and you will see me; I shall greet everyone again, then your heart can rejoice. Laughter fits such reunions. Because some have seen firsthand, they believe; others who never looked remain welcome. Keep describing that meeting, since somebody elsewhere may recognize their own story."

Joy often returns when separated friends meet again. Share your experience even if people laugh, because one person could find comfort there.

When you thought of the claim that one video game may be the last ever built at such a huge scale of time and money, and of the line that artificial intelligence is improving so fast that even people who doubted are being won over, I thought of these three things:

From the Claude Bible set:

The whole earth spoke one language. Heaven remarked, "Now nothing will be withheld which they intend to do." Yet God scattered them abroad, so perhaps each person carries words others need. For today people see truth in part; once whatever is complete has come, giant projects may fade. "Look, all things are being made new," says a voice; first attempts have passed away.

People working together can build almost anything, yet giant projects tend to fade. I believe each human voice matters longer, so keep speaking even after being scattered.

Those disciples watched, but some doubted. Doubters often hear blame because of unbelief; I hope leaders welcome questions so fewer people get scolded. Still God says, "Watch me do this new thing." Every age has its season for building up, one where things break down, and a time to speak: so voice your heart, since another generation comes afterward.

⠀

Doubt asks whether something new can be trusted, though doubters frequently get blamed. Silence need not last; keep expressing yourself because later people might understand.

From the Jesus Bible set:

Heaven and earth may pass away, yet each human voice matters; winemakers put new wine into fresh skins, though anyone tasting old vintage immediately desires it again. Whenever faith runs low, keep speaking your heart even if crowds dismiss you, because whoever trusts me can do greater works than these."

⠀

I do not count size as worth. A person sharing true feeling may get ignored, yet continuing matters because somebody else could finally feel understood.

When employers pay too little for buying land or rest, weariness tells workers that effort is being drained. Wanting your own shade and roof deserves saying out loud.

# Bible quote builder: best outputs

These paragraphs are remixed from World English Bible phrases by an AI model (Claude) under rules set by the repository owner and the paragraphs are not exact Bible quotes.
Words in italics were added or changed by the AI model and words in upright type come from the Bible phrases.
The second paragraph under each remix is a plain explanation written by the AI model and the file named best-outputs-spaced.txt in this folder holds the same text without italics for copying.

## Input: A post that said the whole earth should be destroyed and that the writer has nothing left to live for (the wording of the post is softened here)

*When you thought of saying that the whole earth may as well be destroyed because nothing feels worth living for anymore, I thought of these six things:*

Words in italics were added or changed by the AI model and the second attempt from the Claude Bible set was made before First and Second Corinthians moved into My Personal Bible set.

From the Claude Bible set (attempt 1):

In the middle of *a* valley *lay countless skeletons;* they were very dry. *People* say, "Our bones are dried *out;* hope is lost; we *feel* completely cut off." *Nobody mocked that cry. Instead, one voice asked,* "Can these *ever* live?" *Then* breath came, *sinew returned, flesh grew; each person* lived *again* and stood up on *tired* feet.

*Saying 'nothing is left' out loud took courage. Pain this heavy deserves an answer, not mockery; I hope someone who sees your words answers you.*

From the Claude Bible set (attempt 2):

*One writer said,* "We are pressed *by trouble* on every side, yet not crushed; perplexed *without total* despair; struck down *but never* destroyed." *Another admitted,* "My soul still remembers *bitterness* and is bowed *low* within me. *A single thought comes back* to mind; therefore I have hope: *mercies arrive* new *each* morning."

*Feeling crushed tells how heavy the load is. Those writers named their misery first, then found one small reason; I share their words here for anybody who is hurting.*

From the Claude Bible set (attempt 3):

# Bible quote builder: corrections

This page lists lines that an AI model (Claude) wrote for the Bible quote builder and that the repository owner flagged as wrong on 11 November 2026 and 12 November 2026. Each entry shows the line before the fix and the line after the fix and the reason for the fix. The page exists because two lines that both sound caring can differ in whether the line helps or hurts a reader and a matched pair shows where the edge is.

The quoted lines keep their own punctuation. The numbers in brackets point to the rule on the page named rules.md in this folder.

## Emotions come first [rule 33]

**Before:** tiredness without reward makes sense  
**After:** tiredness warns that toil without reward wastes human strength  
**Why:** the words "makes sense" give tiredness a pat on the head and never say what the tiredness is telling the worker and a reader could even hear approval for toil that brings no reward.

**Before:** disliking labor which purchases neither house nor travel is understandable  
**After:** dislike of labor which purchases neither house nor travel signals missing reward  
**Why:** the word "understandable" is a bare verdict that leaves the reader guessing what is being approved.

**Before:** joyless work holds no mystery  
**After:** joylessness at work reports something true: effort returns too little  
**Why:** the first line explains the feeling from a distance and the second line says what the feeling points toward.

**Before:** feeling crushed does not prove life is over  
**After:** feeling crushed tells how heavy the load is  
**Why:** the first line argues against the feeling and the second line treats the feeling as a report.

**Before:** fear need not win  
**After:** fear deserves hearing since rent stays due  
**Why:** the first line tells fear to lose and the second line gives fear a hearing and names the reason for the fear in the same sentence.

**Before:** doubt is normal whenever something new appears  
**After:** doubt asks whether something new can be trusted  
**Why:** the word "normal" is a bare verdict and the second line says what doubt is doing.

**Before:** my soul is exceedingly sorrowful  
**After:** my soul is exceedingly sorrowful, since death drew near  
**Why:** an emotion word that stands alone gives the reader a label with no reason.

**Before:** therefore dont be afraid  
**After:** therefore dont be afraid alone  
**Why:** the first line tells fear to stop and the second line offers company to a frightened person.

**Before:** if dread speaks, reply, "get behind me, satan"  
**After:** if cruelty speaks, reply, "get behind me, satan"  
**Why:** the first line sends dread away as an enemy and dread is an emotion that deserves a hearing.

**Before:** now pull grief up by its roots  
**After:** now tend grief gently by its roots  
**Why:** the first line treats grief as a weed to rip out.

**Before:** I hope people near an angry person ask something similar.  
**After:** I hope people near a person who is angry ask something similar.  
**Why:** nearly every human being feels anger at some time and the label "an angry person" makes a passing emotion sound like a fixed quality of one unusual person [rule 50].

## No orders and no hopes aimed at what the reader physically does [rule 35]

**Before:** Tired bodies deserve sleep between attempts; I hope yours gets some.  
**After:** Tiredness after such nights reports how much got spent; I hope people see that cost.  
**Why:** the reader alone decides when the reader sleeps and a stranger who hands out sleep sounds like a boss or a doctor that nobody asked for.

**Before:** rest your sore leg, then tell everyone how long this took  
**After:** tell everyone how long this took  
**Why:** the first line orders the reader to take a physical action.

**Before:** Go ahead, laugh  
**After:** Whoever wants may laugh  
**Why:** the first line tells the reader to laugh.

**Before:** Visit your neighbor and tell him  
**After:** A neighbor could visit and tell him  
**Why:** the first line tells the reader to go somewhere.

**Before:** Tiredness says: stop pouring strength where nothing stays  
**After:** Tiredness reports strength being poured where nothing stays  
**Why:** the first line gives the reader a stop order.

## High-certainty words need evidence in the same sentence [rule 36]

**Before:** perseverance builds proven character, then hope  
**After:** perseverance growing into soul level resonance with God, then hope  
**Why:** the word "proven" makes the reward of long effort sound like a certificate handed out by a judge and the reward is something a person feels inside.

**Before:** size never proves worth  
**After:** I do not count size as worth  
**Why:** the words "never" and "proves" claim evidence that the sentence does not hold.

**Before:** They will build houses and inhabit them  
**After:** One prophet promised they will build houses and inhabit them  
**Why:** the word "will" needs a named speaker so the reader knows who is making the promise.

**Before:** giant projects fade  
**After:** giant projects may fade  
**Why:** the first line states a guess as a fact.

**Before:** Wisdom shows itself through how a tower helps humans speak  
**After:** I look for wisdom in how a tower helps humans speak  
**Why:** the word "shows" claims proof and the second line says what the speaker does.

## No vulnerability labels and no pushing one group down [rules 38 and 39 and 45]

**Before:** When you make a feast, ask poor people, because rich neighbors might also return that favor.  
**After:** When anyone makes a feast, I hope invitations go widely, so each table gets filled.  
**Why:** the label "poor people" turns human beings into a category that waits for pity and the first line keeps wealthy neighbors at the center as the givers of favors.

**Before:** I hope hiring promises reach janitors, not just executives, since lost wages bring hunger.  
**After:** I hope hiring promises reach everyone, since lost wages bring hunger.  
**Why:** the first line builds two groups and lifts one group by standing on the other group and the word "everyone" leaves nobody out.

**Before:** Those voices merit attention before any executive's promise.  
**After:** May job promises reach everyone, since missing wages bring hunger.  
**Why:** the first line ranks one group of people above another group.

**Before:** displaced drafters  
**After:** drafters whom owners replaced  
**Why:** the second wording names the people whose choice caused the loss of work.

**Before:** I want hungry people fed first  
**After:** neighbors lacking bread  
**Why:** the label "hungry people" names a category and the second wording describes a situation.

**Before:** the storyteller praises patient digging over quick fruit  
**After:** the storyteller honors patient digging  
**Why:** the first line ranks slow workers above quick workers.

**Before:** many young workers earn rent only  
**After:** many workers earn rent only  
**Why:** the word "young" adds nothing to the meaning and splits adults into groups and hints that other adults are left out of the care.

## Hopes name what other people do and never promise anything for the repository owner [rules 43 and 48]

**Before:** I hope things get better  
**After:** I hope employers offer wages big enough for homes.  
**Why:** a hope with no action is a person staring into the distance and the second line names who could do what.

**Before:** I will keep asking builders to choose that.  
**After:** I hope builders choose that.  
**Why:** the first line commits the repository owner to a task that the repository owner never took on.

**Before:** I hope to carry what you wrote to other people so that weight gets heard.  
**After:** I hope someone who sees your words answers you.  
**Why:** the first line still says what the repository owner will do later and the second line names what another person could do.

## No cliffhangers [rule 47]

**Before:** his servants helped with one gentle question  
**After:** his servants said, if the prophet had asked you to do some great thing, wouldnt you have done it?  
**Why:** the first line names a question and leaves the question out of the sentence and a reader should never have to hunt through the paragraph for words that the sentence points at.

## No compression [rules 32 and 49]

**Before:** Workers feared hunger because one day's harvest left them idle.  
**After:** The whole harvest came in at once, so he stopped hiring. Those workers lost their wages and feared hunger.  
**Why:** the first line squeezes three steps into seven words and leaves the reader to rebuild the missing steps alone.

**Before:** torn gear means no bread  
**After:** If it tore, the catch would escape, and their families would go without bread, so fear rose.  
**Why:** the first line is a clipped phrase that a reader has to decode.

**Before:** A flood of results can break one net or fill every boat.  
**After:** The catch was too big for one boat, so the crew called partners.  
**Why:** the first line leans on a picture and the second line says what happened.

**Before:** a handful, with quietness  
**After:** a handful of people, with quietness  
**Why:** a reader could ask "a handful of what?" and two added words lock the meaning in.

**Before:** let this cup pass away  
**After:** let this cup of suffering pass away  
**Why:** a reader could ask "a cup of what?".

**Before:** the last will be first  
**After:** the last workers hired received full pay too  
**Why:** the first line does not say the last of what and the first line also swaps the rank of two groups.

## Story form [rules 40 and 42 and 46]

**Before:** This is my story about hired vineyard workers and my sayings about wages and bread: some landowner found men waiting late and said: Why do you stand here all day idle? They answered: Because no one has hired us.  
**After:** Some landowner found men still standing here all day idle because no one has hired them.  
**Why:** the introduction and the frames with colons sound like a narrator stepping in front of the story again and again.

**Before:** Plainly: the storyteller counts every worker as deserving full pay  
**After:** The storyteller counts every worker as deserving full pay  
**Why:** the starter word is the same narrator chiming in.

**Before:** a body built from six to nine separate sayings where no word at all may repeat  
**After:** one Bible story told from start to finish where small connector words such as "I" and "and" may repeat  
**Why:** a storyteller who cannot say "I" twice cannot say "I did this and then I did that" and the paragraph turns into a row of proverbs with no thread.

**Before:** a body that only names the pain or that jumps straight to comfort  
**After:** a body with a bad beginning and a middle where someone figures out what to do and an ending with a humane and nonviolent action  
**Why:** the three parts carry a reader from the hurt through the thinking to an action that a person can take.

## Grammar [rule 37]

**Before:** He hoped friends may receive him into their houses.  
**After:** He wished friends would receive him into their houses.  
**Why:** the word "hoped" is past and the word "may" is present and a clash in tense makes a reader stop and reread.

**Before:** somebody tells them, "Go in peace," yet nobody gave anything the body needs  
**After:** somebody tells them, "Go in peace," yet nobody gives anything the body needs  
**Why:** the words "tells" and "gave" sat in two different tenses inside one sentence.

## General audience [rule 29]

**Before:** his father ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him  
**After:** his father ran, and hugged him  
**Why:** a hug carries the same warmth and a reader in a public comment section could read a kiss as suggestive.

## Something to do [rule 51]

**Before:** I hope people who hire meet each applicant in person.  
**After:** A person who keeps getting silence can return to one named decision maker many times as she did, and the duty to listen stays with the judge.  
**Why:** a wish about strangers leaves the hurting reader with the same unmet need and no next step.

# Agents that rebuild the Bible out of chopped key phrases

Warning about a wording change: the repository owner replaces the name "yahweh" with the word "god" everywhere in the Bible programs and in the newer results as a personal reading choice that helps the repository owner follow the quotes which means the quotes differ from the World English Bible at every place where the World English Bible prints the name and a reader who wants the original wording can open the World English Bible itself.

Warning about changed wording in the joined Bible passages: the passages that the AI model joined by hand for the Claude selection and the personal selection and the words of Jesus are not exact Bible quotes because the repository owner set rules that allow pronouns such as "he" and "him" and "they" to be deleted or swapped for naming words and allow rarely used names such as the names of little-known cities to be replaced with generic words and allow the word "the" and punctuation marks to be added or removed which means a reader who wants the exact wording needs to open the World English Bible itself.

This page reports an experiment where a program chopped parts of the World English Bible into short key phrases and ten copying agents then tried to put pieces of the text back together.
An AI model (Claude) ran the test on 11 November 2026 and no other person has rerun the test yet which means every result here is a single unconfirmed analysis.

## How the text was chopped

- A key phrase is a short piece of about four words such as "i shall lack nothing" or "in green pastures".
- A program cut the text at punctuation marks and before linking words such as "and" and "for" and "in" and joined any one-word piece to a neighbor because one word alone rarely makes sense.
- Psalm 23 came out as "yahweh is my shepherd / i shall lack nothing / he makes me lie down / in green pastures / he leads me beside still waters / he restores my soul / he guides me / in the paths of righteousness / for his names sake".
- The cutting is done by simple rules and not by understanding which means some pieces are awkward such as "for you are" followed by "with me".

## The three selections

- Claude selection: 2342 different key phrases from 41 well-known passages.
- personal selection: 43694 different key phrases from ten whole books which are Psalms and Proverbs and Ecclesiastes and Isaiah and Jeremiah and Matthew and Mark and Luke and John and Romans.
- Words of Jesus: 7463 different key phrases from the words that red-letter Bibles print in red in Matthew and Mark and Luke and John.

## How the experiment works

- Ten separate agents each start from one random key phrase and every paste copies a string with a chance of adding or swapping or changing one whole key phrase and no deleting.
- A reader gives one point for every pair of neighboring phrases in a string that are also neighbors in the Bible and a small credit for neighbors from the same chapter.
- A string may hold at most 24 key phrases.

## What the agents rebuilt after 1000 minutes of experiment time

Claude selection (about 23 of 24 phrases per agent sat inside a rebuilt stretch):

- [Genesis 1] god called the light day and the darkness he called night there was evening and there was morning
- [Psalm 27] in yahwehs house all the days of my life to see yahwehs beauty and to inquire
- [Matthew 6] but when you do merciful deeds dont let your left hand know what your right hand does so that your merciful deeds may be in secret
- [Matthew 6] neither do they spin yet i tell you that even solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of these
- [John 15] i command these things to you that you may love one another

personal selection (about 18 of 24 phrases per agent sat inside a rebuilt stretch):

- [Psalm 10] and the fatherless break the arm of the wicked
- [Jeremiah 29] when you search for me
- [Mark 5] he said to her daughter cheer up
- [Luke 5] i have not come to call the righteous
- [Luke 12] how god clothes the grass in the field
- [Isaiah 33] but there yahweh will be with us jesus said to him you shall love the lord your god

Words of Jesus (about 22 of 24 phrases per agent sat inside a rebuilt stretch):

- [Matthew 5] before you you are the salt of the earth
- [Matthew 25] good and faithful servant you have been faithful
- [Luke 12] that i have come to give peace in the earth
- [John 17] and they have believed that you sent me i made known to them your name
- [John 17] which you have given me that they may be one
- [Matthew 5] the lord your vows but i tell you love your enemies

## What the experiment showed

- Whole phrases made the output far more readable than whole words or single letters because every unit already makes some sense alone and the agents only had to find the right neighbors.
- The longest rebuilt stretch in every selection was 6 key phrases in a row which is about 25 words.
- Some rebuilt stretches jump between two places in the Bible at a phrase that occurs in both places such as "i tell you" or "jesus said to him" which produced blends such as "the lord your vows but i tell you love your enemies" and "but there yahweh will be with us jesus said to him you shall love the lord your god".
- The jumps happen because the reader checks one pair of neighbors at a time and a common phrase has many true neighbors.
- The large personal selection rebuilt less (18 phrases against 22 or 23) because the chance that a random phrase is the true neighbor of another phrase falls as the list grows.
- The key phrase version ran about 2400000 to 2900000 pastes per second on the test machine which is faster than the word version.

## One agent per selection from a second run with generic words added by hand

The AI model ran the key phrase experiment a second time and took the whole best string of one agent per selection and joined the rebuilt stretches with only the most generic words which means connecting words and reference words such as "those" and "him" and pointing words such as "here" and "over there" and no new action words or thing words.
Every added word is marked with stars and the stretches stay in the order of the Bible.

Claude selection (all eleven stretches came from Matthew 5):

- for they shall inherit the earth blessed are those *here* for great is your reward in heaven *and those* who are in the house *with him* who is in heaven for that is how *and so* to the ancient ones you shall not make false vows but i tell you dont swear *at him* who is angry with his brother while you are with him on the way *there so* pluck it out and throw it away for it is more profitable for you *than those others* if anyone sues you to take away your coat

personal selection (stretches from Psalm 24 and Psalm 89 and Proverbs 8 and Isaiah 52 and Matthew 9 and Matthew 12):

- and those who were before you in that day says yahweh of armies yahweh says *to them* before your face who will prepare your way before you most certainly i tell you *this* by the way for the sword of the enemy *over there and* from there says yahweh with the sword *to those others* and sinners jesus answered them i told you *so when* they asked him what then are you elijah he said *that to them*

Words of Jesus (stretches from Matthew 5 and 6 and 11 and 17 and 25):

- for they shall inherit the earth blessed are those who have been persecuted *here* before you most certainly i tell you if you have faith with him then he will sit on the throne of his glory *and those* who hate you bless those *others* on the earth i wish it were already kindled *there* in the marketplaces *and not* the best seats in the synagogues *for those* with you how long will i bear with you for everyone *here* and traded with them i tell you and much more *than that*

What the joined key phrase strings show:

- Each string needed only 6 to 8 added word groups to read as one passage because each rebuilt stretch is already several words of real Bible text.
- The joined key phrase strings read far more like a sermon than the joined word strings did because whole stretches such as "blessed are those who have been persecuted" arrive intact.
- The meaning of each joined string is new and belongs to no Bible passage because the stretches come from different verses and the added words are choices made by the AI model.

## The same three strings with the stretches rearranged into the most sensible order

The repository owner then allowed the AI model to drop the chapter labels and to put the rebuilt stretches in any order and to add the same generic words as before (connecting words and reference words and pointing words) with the goal of the most sensible sounding passage.
The words inside each stretch stay in Bible order and every added word is marked with stars.

Claude selection:

- *to those* who are in the house *and to him* who is angry with his brother while you are with him on the way *and* to the ancient ones you shall not make false vows but i tell you dont swear *and* if anyone sues you to take away your coat pluck it out and throw it away for it is more profitable for you for great is your reward in heaven *with him* who is in heaven for that is how *those before you* for they shall inherit the earth blessed are those

personal selection:

- they asked him what then are you elijah he said *to them* and sinners jesus answered them i told you *of him* before your face who will prepare your way before you most certainly i tell you *that he* and those who were before you in that day says yahweh of armies yahweh says *this* from there says yahweh with the sword *so not* by the way for the sword of the enemy

Words of Jesus:

- with you how long will i bear with you for everyone *there* in the marketplaces the best seats in the synagogues and traded with them i tell you and much more *yet those* who hate you bless those *others* for they shall inherit the earth blessed are those who have been persecuted *here* before you most certainly i tell you if you have faith with him then he will sit on the throne of his glory *over all those* on the earth i wish it were already kindled

What rearranging changed:

- Free order let each string open with a scene and close with a blessing or a wish which the Bible order could not do because Bible order is fixed by chapter number.
- The personal selection gained the most because the six stretches became one exchange (a question and an answer and a promise and a warning) where Bible order had scattered the speakers.
- Every added word in the three strings is a connecting word or a reference word or a pointing word which means no new action word or thing word entered any string.

## Five versions of one words of Jesus string graded against the writing rules in this folder

The AI model took the eight rebuilt stretches of the words of Jesus string above and made five versions and graded each version against the seven sentence rules in the page named writing-rules in the folder named writing-rules.
Each rule earns 0 or 1 or 2 points which gives a top score of 14 and the grades are the judgment of the AI model and no second reader checked the grades.
The seven rules are: a sentence can be understood alone and a reason is attached to each claim and labels are explained and people and things are named in place of pointing words and no short clipped sentences and one claim plus reason per sentence and no commas.

Version 1 (Bible order and nothing added) scored 6 of 14:

- for they shall inherit the earth blessed are those who have been persecuted before you most certainly i tell you if you have faith with him then he will sit on the throne of his glory who hate you bless those on the earth i wish it were already kindled in the marketplaces the best seats in the synagogues with you how long will i bear with you for everyone and traded with them i tell you and much more
- The version lost points because the whole text is one run-on sentence that stacks about eight claims and names nobody.

Version 2 (Bible order with generic joining words) scored 6 of 14:

- for they shall inherit the earth blessed are those who have been persecuted *here* before you most certainly i tell you if you have faith with him then he will sit on the throne of his glory *and those* who hate you bless those *others* on the earth i wish it were already kindled *there* in the marketplaces *and not* the best seats in the synagogues *for those* with you how long will i bear with you for everyone *here* and traded with them i tell you and much more *than that*
- The joining words made the text flow better and the score did not move because none of the seven rules measures flow and the text is still one run-on sentence.

Version 3 (Bible order cut into sentences) scored 7 of 14:

- for they shall inherit the earth blessed are those who have been persecuted *here* before you. most certainly i tell you if you have faith with him then he will sit on the throne of his glory. *and those* who hate you bless those *others* on the earth. i wish it were already kindled *there* in the marketplaces *and in* the best seats in the synagogues. with you how long will i bear with you for everyone *here* and traded with them. i tell you and much more *than that*.
- Sentence breaks raised the score for one claim per sentence and the last sentence became short and clipped which cost a point.

Version 4 (rearranged so that each sentence pairs a claim with a reason) scored 10 of 14:

- with you how long will i bear with you for everyone *there* in the marketplaces *and in* the best seats in the synagogues *because those* and traded with them i tell you and much more. *those* who hate you bless those *others* for they shall inherit the earth blessed are those who have been persecuted *here* before you. most certainly i tell you if you have faith with him then he will sit on the throne of his glory *over all those*. on the earth i wish it were already kindled *for all of those here*.
- Rearranging let every sentence carry a claim and a reason joined by "because" or "for" or "if" and removed the clipped sentence.

Version 5 (reference words tied to a group named in the same sentence) scored 11 of 14:

- with you how long will i bear with you for everyone *there* in the marketplaces *and in* the best seats in the synagogues *because those same ones* and traded with them i tell you and much more. *those* who hate you bless those *same ones* for they shall inherit the earth blessed are those who have been persecuted *here* before you. most certainly i tell you if you have faith with him then he will sit on the throne of his glory *over everyone*. on the earth i wish it were already kindled *because of all of you here*.
- Tying "those same ones" to "everyone in the marketplaces" and to "those who hate you" earned one point for naming.

Why the score stops at 11:

- The rule about naming people and things asks for names in place of pointing words while the joining rule from the repository owner allows only pointing words and other generic words which means the two rules pull against each other.
- The words "him" and "he" and "it" in the stretches point at someone or something the stretches never name and no generic word can supply the name.
- The label "throne of his glory" stays unexplained because an explanation would need new thing words.

## One finished passage per selection made the same way as version 5

The AI model took the best string of a second agent from each selection and went straight to the method of version 5 which means free order and sentence breaks and a claim with a reason in each sentence and generic words only.
Every added word is marked with stars and the grades use the same seven rules with a top score of 14.

Claude selection (10 of 14) from the stretches "on the earth there was evening" and "herbs yielding seed after their kind and it was so god saw everything" and "who mourn for they shall be comforted" and "and be exceedingly glad for great is your reward in heaven" and "who were before you you are the salt of the earth" and "who is in secret" and "at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery" and "yes and your no be no" and "who is evil but whoever strikes you" and "you shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy":

- on the earth there was evening *and* herbs yielding seed after their kind and it was so god saw everything. *those* who mourn for they shall be comforted *here* and be exceedingly glad for great is your reward in heaven. *those* who were before you you are the salt of the earth *for him* who is in secret. *anyone here* at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery *so* yes and your no be no. *as for him* who is evil but whoever strikes you *then* you shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy *no longer*.

personal selection (9 of 14) from the stretches "in heart if the foundations are destroyed" and "i have set yahweh always before me whose sandal strap im" and "who rose up against me and by" and "in labor they will look on him" and "who has had boldness to approach me says yahweh shouldnt my soul be avenged" and "neither has he gone into captivity" and "the kingdom of heaven is at hand":

- i have set yahweh always before me whose sandal strap im *under because* the kingdom of heaven is at hand. *even* in heart if the foundations are destroyed neither has he gone into captivity *with those* who rose up against me and by *them*. in labor they will look on him who has had boldness to approach me says yahweh *for* shouldnt my soul be avenged.

Words of Jesus (10 of 14) from the stretches "they persecuted the prophets who were" and "and whoever says you fool will be" and "and not sacrifice for i came not" and "on an old garment for the patch would tear away" and "women there has not arisen anyone greater than john the baptizer" and "for you to enter into gods kingdom before you most certainly i tell you i havent found" and "even the chosen ones behold i have told you beforehand" and "and prepare a place for you":

- they persecuted the prophets who were *before you and* even the chosen ones behold i have told you beforehand. women there has not arisen anyone greater than john the baptizer *yet* for you to enter into gods kingdom before you most certainly i tell you i havent found *anyone here*. *for all of you* and not sacrifice for i came not on an old garment for the patch would tear away. *here with you* and prepare a place for you *yet* and whoever says you fool will be *apart from all of you*.

Notes on the three passages:

- The Claude selection passage scored 10 because five sentences each carry a claim and a reason while "him who is in secret" and "him who is evil" name nobody.
- The words "no longer" were added to the stretch "you shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy" because the stretch quotes an old saying that the speaker in Matthew 5 goes on to reject and the two generic words keep the passage from teaching hatred of an enemy.
- The personal selection passage scored 9 because the stretches came from six different books and three of the stretches were cut in the middle of a thought such as "whose sandal strap im" and "who rose up against me and by".
- The line "shouldnt my soul be avenged" is a question spoken by yahweh in the book of Jeremiah and the passage keeps the line as a question and does not present harm to any person as good.
- The words of Jesus passage scored 10 because each sentence pairs a claim with "yet" or "for" while "for all of you and not sacrifice" lacks the thing that is wanted in place of sacrifice which is the word "mercy" in the source.

## The same passages after the repository owner allowed naming words that already appear in the string

The repository owner widened the joining rule so that the AI model could also add a naming word such as "the earth" or "god" or "the synagogues" as long as that naming word already appears somewhere in the same string which means no person or thing from outside the string enters the passage.
Every added word is marked with stars and the grades use the same seven rules with a top score of 14.

Version 6 of the words of Jesus string from the five-version section (12 of 14 and up from 11):

- with you how long will i bear with you for everyone *there* in the marketplaces *and in* the best seats in the synagogues *because those in the synagogues* and traded with them i tell you and much more. *those* who hate you bless those *in the marketplaces* for they shall inherit the earth blessed are those who have been persecuted *on the earth* before you. most certainly i tell you if you have faith with him then he will sit on the throne of his glory *over the earth*. on the earth i wish it were already kindled *this faith in all of you here*.

Claude selection (12 of 14 and up from 10):

- on the earth there was evening *and* herbs yielding seed after their kind and it was so god saw everything. *those* who mourn for they shall be comforted *on the earth* and be exceedingly glad for great is your reward in heaven. *those* who were before you you are the salt of the earth *for god* who is in secret. *anyone* at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery *so* yes and your no be no *before god*. *as for the enemy* who is evil but whoever strikes you *then* you shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy *no longer*.

personal selection (10 of 14 and up from 9):

- i have set yahweh always before me whose sandal strap im *under because* the kingdom of heaven is at hand. *even* in heart if the foundations *of the kingdom* are destroyed neither has he gone into captivity *with those* who rose up against me and by *their boldness against yahweh*. in labor they will look on him who has had boldness to approach me says yahweh *for* shouldnt my soul be avenged.

Words of Jesus (12 of 14 and up from 10):

- they persecuted the prophets who were *before you and* even the chosen ones behold i have told you beforehand. *among* women there has not arisen anyone greater than john the baptizer *yet* for you to enter into gods kingdom before you most certainly i tell you i havent found *a place*. *a place for the chosen ones* and not sacrifice for i came not on an old garment for the patch would tear away *the garment*. *in gods kingdom* and prepare a place for you *yet* and whoever says you fool will be *apart from gods kingdom*.

What the naming words changed:

- Reused naming words lifted every score by 1 or 2 points because phrases such as "god who is in secret" and "the enemy who is evil" and "apart from gods kingdom" now say who or what a sentence is about.
- The personal selection gained the least because the seven stretches share few naming words and the words "he" and "him" inside the stretches still point at people the stretches never name.
- Reused naming words also let the AI model steer meaning more strongly than generic words could (for example "this faith in all of you here" decides what "it" refers to) which means the passages now carry more of the choices of the AI model and less of the chance output of the agents.

## A special rule for the words of Jesus selection: the names of the speaker and of God may be added freely

The repository owner added a rule for the words of Jesus selection only: the AI model may add "the father" and "jesus" and "the christ" and "god" and "yahweh" wherever a sentence needs one of those names even when the name appears nowhere in the string.
Every added word is marked with stars and the grades use the same seven rules with a top score of 14.

First string (13 of 14 and up from 12):

- with you how long will i *jesus* bear with you for everyone *there* in the marketplaces *and in* the best seats in the synagogues *because those in the synagogues* and traded with them i tell you and much more. *those* who hate you bless those *in the marketplaces* for they shall inherit the earth blessed are those who have been persecuted *on the earth* before you. most certainly i tell you if you have faith with him *the christ* then he will sit on the throne of his glory *beside the father over the earth*. on the earth i wish it were already kindled *this faith in god in all of you here*.

Second string (13 of 14 and up from 12):

- they persecuted the prophets who were *before you and* even the chosen ones *of god* behold i *jesus* have told you beforehand. *among* women there has not arisen anyone greater than john the baptizer *yet* for you to enter into gods kingdom before you most certainly i tell you i havent found *a place apart from the father*. *the father and* not sacrifice for i *the christ* came not on an old garment for the patch would tear away *the garment*. *with the father in gods kingdom* and prepare a place for you *yet* and whoever says you fool will be *apart from god*.

What the special rule changed:

- The names closed the gap that no earlier rule could close because "i" now has the name "jesus" beside the word and "him" and "he" now have "the christ" beside the words.
- Both strings reached 13 of 14 and the one missing point comes from labels that stay unexplained such as "the throne of his glory".
- The special rule applies to one selection only which means the scores of the words of Jesus passages can no longer be compared fairly with the scores of the other two selections.
- The AI model chose which name goes with each "he" and "him" from knowledge of the source verses and a wrong choice would put words about one person onto another person.

## Special words of three kinds may fill the gaps: naming words and action words and describing words

The repository owner widened the joining rule again so that each selection has a list of special words that may be added in any gap even when the special word appears nowhere in the string.
The AI model counted every word in each selection and then sorted the most used words by hand into naming words and action words and describing words and kept about 12 of each kind.
Only the exact listed form of a word was used which means "made" is allowed in a selection where "made" is listed while "makes" is not allowed.
The word "seed" was added to the words of Jesus list because the repository owner named the word and not because the word ranks high by count and the word "love" ranks about 38th by count in the words of Jesus (44 uses).

Claude selection special words:

- Naming words: god and yahweh and love and earth and father and time and day and heaven and man and light and son and heart.
- Action words: made and give and know and tell and saw and see and keep and heard and called and seek and put and make.
- Describing words: good and evil and blessed and right and great and holy and wicked and righteous and secret and perfect and living and new.

personal selection special words:

- Naming words: yahweh and god and man and jesus and son and people and lord and day and king and house and land and heart.
- Action words: says and know and tell and give and see and say and made and make and take and heard and hear and answered.
- Describing words: good and evil and great and wicked and righteous and holy and high and right and wise and blessed and dead and poor.

Words of Jesus special words:

- Naming words: father and man and son and god and kingdom and lord and heaven and world and house and life and day and earth and love and seed plus the names jesus and christ and yahweh from the earlier special rule.
- Action words: tell and see and know and give and sent and say and hear and take and believe and enter and receive and made.
- Describing words: good and evil and little and great and blessed and greater and dead and eternal and last and righteous and right and full.

The same four strings as the last two sections were joined again by hand with the wider rule and every added word is marked with stars.
The grades use the same seven rules with a top score of 14 and the AI model graded passages that the AI model wrote which means the grades are a rough guide and not an outside measurement.

Words of Jesus first string (14 of 14 and up from 13):

- with you how long will i *jesus* bear with you for everyone in the marketplaces *and in* the best seats in the synagogues *made the house of god a house of the world* and traded with them i tell you and much more. *the father sent love to those* who hate you *so* bless those *in the marketplaces* for they shall inherit the earth blessed are those who have been persecuted *for the kingdom* before you. most certainly i tell you if you have faith with him *the christ* then he will sit on the throne of his glory *which the father made great in heaven*. on the earth i wish it were already kindled *the good seed of love that the father sent to the world*.

Words of Jesus second string (14 of 14 and up from 13):

- they persecuted the prophets who were *sent* before you and even the chosen ones *of god* behold i *jesus* have told you beforehand. *among* women there has not arisen anyone greater than john the baptizer *yet* for you to enter into gods kingdom before you most certainly i tell you i havent found *a place apart from the father*. *the father sent the son to give love* and not sacrifice for i *the christ* came not on an old garment for the patch would tear away *the garment*. *believe so the father and the son enter the house in heaven* and prepare a place for you *yet* and whoever says you fool will be *last in the kingdom*.

Claude selection (13 of 14 and up from 12):

- on the earth there was evening *and god made* herbs yielding seed after their kind and it was so god saw everything *good*. *blessed are those* who mourn for they shall be comforted *on the earth* and be exceedingly glad for great is your reward in heaven. *the righteous* who were before you *heard* you are the salt of the earth *from the father* who is in secret. *a man who saw evil* at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery *in the heart so keep your yes* yes and your no be no *before god*. *god saw the man* who is evil but whoever strikes you *give the man love because* you shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy *no longer*.

personal selection (12 of 14 and up from 10):

- i have set yahweh always before me *the great king* whose sandal strap im *under because* the kingdom of heaven is at hand. *the righteous man answered* in heart if the foundations *of the house* are destroyed *the wise people know the righteous man* neither has he gone into captivity *with the wicked people* who rose up against me and by *evil made the land poor*. *the people of the land* in labor they will look on him *the holy king* who has had boldness to approach me says yahweh *and the lord answered* shouldnt my soul be avenged.

What the three kinds of special words changed:

- Action words gave the largest gain because a gap can now hold a full small claim such as "the father sent love to those" where the earlier rules could only hold a pointer such as "those".
- Describing words let a passage say which kind of person a sentence is about such as "the righteous man" and "the wicked people" which is why the personal selection gained 2 points after gaining the least under every earlier rule.
- Both words of Jesus strings reached the top score while the gain was only 1 point each because the earlier rule had already lifted both strings to 13.
- The added words now carry a large share of the meaning (for example "the father sent the son to give love" stands where the source verse has "i desire mercy") which means the passages read more like sentences written by the AI model around Bible fragments than like chance output of the agents.
- The ending "last in the kingdom" is milder than the source verse about the word "fool" and that mildness is a choice of the AI model and not a finding.
- The line "shouldnt my soul be avenged" stays a question spoken by yahweh in the book of Jeremiah and the passage does not present harm to any person as good.

What the program does with the same lists:

- The live program now lets agents place single joining words from the generic list and from the special list of the chosen selection and the reader gives credit when the word before the joining word and the word after the joining word each sit beside the joining word somewhere in the source.
- In one run of 6 million pastes per selection the agents kept mostly generic joining words such as "and" and "there" and "with them" and almost no special words because the two-sided check is easier to pass for very common words.
- The average count of phrases inside rebuilt stretches per agent was 29.4 for the Claude selection and 15.5 for the personal selection and 21.0 for the words of Jesus.
- The joining words chosen by the program read as filler because the program checks word pairs and has no test of meaning which means the hand joining above is still far ahead of the program.

## One chapter against one chapter: John 10 and Psalm 88

The repository owner asked for the same process on two single chapters which means the key phrase cutting and the evolution run and the special word lists and the hand joining were all repeated on John chapter 10 and on Psalm 88 from the World English Bible.

Size of each source:

- John 10 holds 799 words that the cutting rule turned into 193 different key phrases.
- Psalm 88 holds 288 words that the cutting rule turned into 75 different key phrases.

What the agents did in a run of 3 million pastes per chapter:

- Every agent in both chapters ended with all 32 pieces inside rebuilt stretches because a single chapter has so few phrases that finding true neighbors is easy (the whole-book selections reached only about 15 to 29 of 32).
- The agents dropped every joining word in both chapters because a rebuilt phrase pair earns more credit than a joining word and a small source always offers a rebuilt pair.
- The best John 10 string held 13 short stretches and the best Psalm 88 string held 11 short stretches and the longest stretch was 6 phrases in both chapters which means the agents shuffled the chapter into short true pieces and did not rebuild the chapter in order.

Special words for John 10 with counts:

- Naming words: sheep 16 and father 11 and shepherd 6 and jesus 6 and hand 6 and voice 5 and life 5 and works 5 and door 4 and jews 4 and god 3 and demon 3.
- Action words: know 6 and believe 6 and lay 4 and answered 4 and tell 3 and listen 3 and follow 3 and hear 2 and take 2 and snatch 2.
- Describing words: good 5 and hired 3 and own and eternal and true and blind.

Special words for Psalm 88 with counts:

- Naming words: yahweh 4 and day 2 and prayer 2 and soul 2 and pit 2 and grave 2 and wrath 2 and friends 2 and wonders 2 and terrors 2 and god 1 and night 1.
- Action words: cried 2 and made 2 and cut 2 and remember and turn and enter and show and rise and praise and spread and reject and hide.
- Describing words: dead 2 and afflicted 2 and full and dim and dark and lowest and darkest and fierce and near and loving.

John 10 joined by hand from the best string of agent 1 (13 of 14) with added words marked by stars:

- *jesus answered the jews* as i told you my sheep hear my voice and i know them and they follow me i give eternal life to them. the good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep *because the sheep know the voice of the shepherd* whenever he brings out his own sheep he goes *to the door*. *the jews answered* and said to him how long will you hold us for they dont know the voice of strangers jesus spoke this parable to them but they didnt understand. jesus therefore said to them again most certainly *no one can take the sheep out* of my fathers hand i and the father are one. *so the jews take* stones again to stone him jesus answered them *for which of the good* works do you stone me the jews answered him we dont stone you *for good works*. *jesus answered* if i dont do the works of my father *do not believe* but if i do them though you dont believe me believe the works. others said these are not the sayings of one possessed *by a demon because the works are good*.

Psalm 88 joined by hand from the best string of agent 1 (12 of 14) with added words marked by stars:

- The John 10 passage reports that people picked up stones and the passage keeps the question "for which of the good works do you stone me" as a question which means the passage does not present harm to any person as good.

## Newest rules: one word for God everywhere and adjacent pronouns may be deleted and punctuation may be added

The repository owner made three rule changes at once:

- The name "yahweh" is now always replaced by the word "god" in every selection and every Bible program because the repository owner wants one word for God (this is a personal reading choice and the warning at the top of this page says so).
- When the AI model adds a naming word right beside a pronoun the AI model may delete that pronoun so that "i *jesus* bear with you" becomes "*jesus* bear with you" because the doubled wording reads badly.
- The AI model may add periods and commas and question marks and quote marks and other neutral break marks wherever a break helps a reader because the key phrase cutting had removed every mark.

Every added word is still marked with stars and every deleted pronoun is listed under the passage and punctuation marks are not starred because every mark in these passages was added by the AI model.
The grades use the same seven rules with a top score of 14 and the AI model graded passages that the AI model wrote which means the grades are a rough guide.

## Grammar rule: a word may change form when a naming word replaces a pronoun

The repository owner added a smoothing rule for every selection: when a naming word replaces a pronoun and the swap breaks the grammar the AI model may change the form of the nearby word so that the sentence stays correct (for example "i have told you" becomes "*jesus has* told you" because "jesus have told you" reads wrongly).
A changed word is marked with stars the same way an added word is marked.

Where the rule changed a passage in the section above:

- Words of Jesus second string: "behold, i *jesus* have told you beforehand" became "behold, *jesus has* told you beforehand".
- personal selection first fresh string: the opening "*the wise man says to god:* i have sworn" became "*the wise man has* sworn *to god*".
- The other seven passages needed no change because every swap in those passages already left correct grammar (for example "how long will *jesus* bear with you" is correct because the word "will" takes the plain form "bear").
- Both changed passages keep the same grade because the grades were already counting those sentences as understandable and the change removes an awkward spot without adding meaning.
- The rule also widens what the pronoun deletion rule can do because a pronoun that could not be deleted before (such as the "i" in "i have told") can now be replaced.

## Speaker rule for the words of Jesus: the passages are read as spoken by Christ

The repository owner added a rule for the words of Jesus selection only: every passage is read as spoken by Christ which means the added words avoid the name "jesus" because the speaker in the four gospels rarely uses that name for himself and more often says "i" or "the son of man".
The word "i" now stays as the source has the word and "the son of man" stands where a "he" or "him" points at the speaker and the name "jesus" was removed from the special word list of the live program for this selection.
The grades assume a reader who knows that Christ is speaking because the rule itself sets that assumption.
