# How the outputs of the Bible quote builder evolved step by step

This page shows one sample output from each stage of the Bible quote builder so that a visitor can watch the outputs change from noise into readable paragraphs.
The Bible quote builder is a working name for an experiment where ten copying agents paste pieces of the World English Bible together while a simple reader favors strings that match the Bible and an AI model (Claude) then joins the result by hand under rules that the repository owner set one at a time.
Every sample comes from the words of Jesus in the four gospels unless the line says otherwise because following one selection makes the change from stage to stage easy to see.
Added or changed words carry stars from stage 4 onward and the scores use seven sentence rules from the page named writing-rules in the folder named writing-rules with a top score of 14.
The AI model graded outputs that the AI model wrote which means the scores are a rough guide and not an outside measurement.

Warning about changed wording: the later samples are not exact Bible quotes because the rules allow added words and swapped pronouns and replaced names and added punctuation and the name "yahweh" is always replaced by the word "god" which means a reader who wants the exact wording needs to open the World English Bible itself.

## Stage 1: agents copy single letters

- The agents changed one letter at a time and the reader gave credit for getting close to a short Bible quote.
- The method could finish short quotes such as "love your enemies" and became far too slow for large quote lists (about 100 to 500 pastes per second).
- No sample is shown because the strings were mostly half-built words.

## Stage 2: agents copy whole words

- Sample: "when you pray / as in heaven / but sinners to repentance / word of the kingdom / but know this / and not perceive / given to god / and to return / distress in the land / but you dont believe"
- Each piece between the slashes is a real Bible fragment of three or four words and the pieces have nothing to do with each other because the reader only checked whether each piece was a real quote.

## Stage 3: agents copy key phrases of about four words

- Sample of rebuilt stretches: "before you you are the salt of the earth" and "good and faithful servant you have been faithful" and "and they have believed that you sent me i made known to them your name"
- The reader now gave a point for every pair of neighboring phrases that are also neighbors in the Bible so the agents rebuilt true stretches of up to about 25 words.

## Stage 4: the stretches are joined by hand with generic words only (6 of 14)

- for they shall inherit the earth blessed are those who have been persecuted *here* before you most certainly i tell you if you have faith with him then he will sit on the throne of his glory *and those* who hate you bless those *others* on the earth i wish it were already kindled *there* in the marketplaces *and not* the best seats in the synagogues *for those* with you how long will i bear with you for everyone *here* and traded with them i tell you and much more *than that*
- Only connecting words and pointing words were allowed and the stretches stayed in Bible order which left one long run-on sentence.

## Stage 5: free order and sentence breaks and a reason in every sentence (10 of 14)

- with you how long will i bear with you for everyone *there* in the marketplaces *and in* the best seats in the synagogues *because those* and traded with them i tell you and much more. *those* who hate you bless those *others* for they shall inherit the earth blessed are those who have been persecuted *here* before you. most certainly i tell you if you have faith with him then he will sit on the throne of his glory *over all those*. on the earth i wish it were already kindled *for all of those here*.
- Rearranging the stretches let every sentence carry a claim and a reason.

## Stage 6: naming words that already appear in the string may be reused (12 of 14)

- with you how long will i bear with you for everyone *there* in the marketplaces *and in* the best seats in the synagogues *because those in the synagogues* and traded with them i tell you and much more. *those* who hate you bless those *in the marketplaces* for they shall inherit the earth blessed are those who have been persecuted *on the earth* before you. most certainly i tell you if you have faith with him then he will sit on the throne of his glory *over the earth*. on the earth i wish it were already kindled *this faith in all of you here*.
- Phrases such as "those in the synagogues" now say who a sentence is about.

## Stage 7: special naming words and action words and describing words may fill the gaps (14 of 14)

- with you how long will i *jesus* bear with you for everyone in the marketplaces *and in* the best seats in the synagogues *made the house of god a house of the world* and traded with them i tell you and much more. *the father sent love to those* who hate you *so* bless those *in the marketplaces* for they shall inherit the earth blessed are those who have been persecuted *for the kingdom* before you. most certainly i tell you if you have faith with him *the christ* then he will sit on the throne of his glory *which the father made great in heaven*. on the earth i wish it were already kindled *the good seed of love that the father sent to the world*.
- Each selection received about 12 of its most used naming words and action words and describing words and an action word lets a gap hold a whole small claim such as "the father sent love to those".

## Stage 8: punctuation and pronoun deletion and grammar changes and the speaker rule (14 of 14)

- "with you, how long will i bear with you? for everyone in the marketplaces, *and in* the best seats in the synagogues, *made the house of god a house of the world* and traded with them, i tell you, and much more. *the father sent love to those* who hate you, *so* bless those *in the marketplaces*, for they shall inherit the earth. blessed are those who have been persecuted *for the kingdom* before you. most certainly i tell you, if you have faith with *the son of man*, then he will sit on the throne of his glory, *which the father made great in heaven*. on the earth, i wish it were already kindled: *the good seed of love that the father sent to the world*."
- Periods and commas and question marks and quote marks were added and a pronoun beside an added name may be deleted and a word may change form to keep the grammar correct and every words of Jesus passage is read as spoken by Christ which is why "the son of man" stands where "jesus" and "the christ" stood in stage 7.

## Stage 9: any pronoun may be swapped for a naming word and rarely used names become generic words (13 of 14 on a fresh string)

- "*the man who hears the father* who is in heaven, *that man* is my brother. *the lord says to the man,* 'well done, good and faithful servant,' and give *the kingdom* to *the servant* who has the ten talents. *the man who loves the world more* than me is not worthy of me, and *the man* who doesnt have *love*, even that which he has will be taken away from him. *the father had a son, and the father* sent *the son* last to *the farmers*, saying, '*the farmers* will respect my son.' but the farmers *did not receive the son*. *it will be right* for *two foreign cities* in the judgment with this generation, *because this generation saw the son and did not believe*. *love your father* and your mother; you still lack one thing: *give to the little ones and enter the kingdom*."
- Pronouns may also be added or deleted anywhere in every selection when the change helps a reader.
- The source stretch read "he sent him last to them saying they will respect my son" and now names the father and the son and the farmers and the city names "tyre and sidon" became "two foreign cities".

## Stage 10: a fresh paragraph from each selection under every rule

Claude selection of 41 well-known passages (13 of 14):

- *lord god,* in all the earth you have set your *light, and* you have put all things under *the* feet *of man:* all sheep *and every living thing*. *keep what is holy, and* neither throw your pearls before the pigs. *whatever a man says more* than *what is right* is of the evil one. you have heard that it was said, "you shall not commit adultery," but i tell you, love your enemies, *because* a good tree cant produce evil fruit, neither can a corrupt *tree make good fruit*. *blessed are the righteous* for righteousness sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven; *not the man who says "lord,"* but he who does the will of my father who is in heaven, for *the father* makes his sun to rise *on the evil and the good*.

personal selection of ten whole books (11 of 14):

- the assembly of the elders of the people were gathered together in jerusalem, because you have said, "praise be to god." god, i have called *on you from a small town across the river, and god hears* when *the poor man* cries, for *god* commands *the king to give* with justice. "*evil will not take the land* from the north," says god, for god says, "*do not take your heart* from me," says god, "for i am with you," says god. god said to me, "*make the land* like *a high green land, and give the good of the land* to take back to those *poor people*."

## Side experiment: John 10 dealt into four random piles

- The 201 key phrases of John chapter 10 were dealt at random into four piles and the AI model built one paragraph from every phrase in each pile.
- Each pile came out as a small version of the whole chapter because the chapter repeats its main ideas and about one word in three had to be added.
- Three full remixes (twelve paragraphs) are on the page named john-10-remixes in this folder.

## Side experiment: sixteen random phrases kept in a random order

- Sixteen key phrases were drawn at random from the ten whole books of the personal selection and shuffled three times and the AI model connected the phrases in the exact shuffled order with no sorting.
- Each of the three passages reads as a short connected scene and about half of the words in each passage had to be added and the three passages tell three different stories.
- The three passages are on the page named full-record in this folder in the section about sixteen random phrases.

## Stage 11: every word different and an open vocabulary on random phrases in a random order

Claude selection (12 of 14 with 58 different words out of 58 words) from the eight phrases in this drawn order: "before you" and "that he" and "whoever shall put away his wife" and "if only you god" and "ask of the father" and "for they think" and "than these is of the evil one" and "dont sound a trumpet":

- *mercy walks* before *every traveler, so* that he *who stumbles finds welcome.* whoever shall put away his wife *must first weigh her sorrow.* if only you, god, *would soften hard hearts!* ask of *your* father *plainly,* for *proud people* think *louder prayers win; anything showier* than these *quiet words* is *from* the evil one. dont sound a trumpet.

personal selection (12 of 14 with 48 different words out of 48 words) from the eight phrases in this drawn order: "they were exceedingly astonished" and "who are these" and "whatever you will ask" and "from a far country yes" and "and a spirit of justice to him" and "his disciples asked him about the parable" and "for justice but behold oppression" and "for those":

- *villagers* were exceedingly astonished: "who are these *strangers?*" "whatever you will ask," *came one reply* from a far country, "yes, and *true* spirit of justice to *any judge.*" his disciples asked him about the parable. "*people hoped* for *fairness,* but behold, oppression *arrived instead; stand alongside* those *crushed.*"

Words of Jesus (13 of 14 with 48 different words out of 48 words) from the eight phrases in this drawn order: "and tell him friend" and "that you dont expect him" and "therefore dont be afraid" and "get behind me satan" and "from one end of" and "sitting in sackcloth" and "in yourselves" and "he doesnt stumble":

- "*visit your neighbor* and tell him, 'friend, *comfort comes at an hour* that you *cannot* expect; therefore dont be afraid.' *if dread speaks, reply,* 'get behind me, satan.' from one end of *earth people mourn,* sitting in sackcloth; *carry light with*in yourselves, *because whoever does so* doesnt stumble."

- Eight phrases were drawn at random from each selection and kept in a random order and the AI model could add almost any English word while keeping every word in the passage different.

## What the ten stages show together

- The scores for one words of Jesus string rose from 6 to 10 to 12 to 14 as the rules widened which means each new rule removed one kind of obstacle for a reader.
- The largest jumps came from free ordering with sentence breaks (6 to 10) and from allowing action words in the gaps (13 to 14 with a much fuller first sentence).
- Every wider rule also moved more of the meaning from the agents to the AI model because the agents only supply true Bible fragments and the AI model chooses the order and the added words and who each pronoun points at.
- The later paragraphs are therefore best read as short compositions built around real Bible fragments and not as quotations or as teaching from the Bible.
- The live programs run stage 3 with single joining words added and do not perform stages 4 to 10 because the programs have no test of meaning or grammar.

## Where the full record is

- The page named full-record in this folder holds every rule and every passage in the order the rules were added.
- The page named bible-selections-word-evolution in this folder holds the stage 2 runs with single words.
- The folder named boring-things at the top of the repository holds the program files for every stage.

# Three remixes of John chapter 10 made by dealing the chapter into four random piles

This page holds three remixes of John chapter 10 from the World English Bible and each remix was made by dealing the 201 key phrases of the chapter at random into four piles the way a deck of cards is dealt and then building one paragraph from every phrase in each pile.
A key phrase is a short piece of about four words such as "i am the good shepherd" and the three remixes differ only in the random order of the deal.
An AI model (Claude) wrote the paragraphs on 11 November 2026 under rules that the repository owner set which allow free order and added joining words and a short list of the most used words of the chapter and changed pronouns and added punctuation and generic words in place of rarely used names.
Added or changed words carry stars and a program check confirmed that every dealt phrase appears in its paragraph except the two place names that were replaced ("beyond the jordan" became "across the river" and "in solomons porch" became "in a covered walkway").
The grades use seven sentence rules from the page named writing-rules in the folder named writing-rules with a top score of 14 and the AI model graded paragraphs that the AI model wrote which means the grades are a rough guide.

Warning about changed wording: these paragraphs are not exact Bible quotes because about one word in three was added by the AI model and pronouns and names were changed which means a reader who wants the exact wording needs to open John chapter 10 in the World English Bible itself.

## Remix 1

Pile 1 (12 of 14 and 30 percent of the words were added):

- it was the feast of the dedication, and jesus was walking in the temple. the jews therefore came around him, *and* jesus spoke this parable to them: "the gatekeeper opens the gate *for the shepherd, and* he goes *in* for the sheep. he who is a hired hand *is not the shepherd,* because he is a hired hand, and a robber *and* the thief only comes to steal, kill. i came for the sheep. i am the good shepherd; i know my own, and im known *by my own*. *the sheep* by no means follow a stranger, for they dont know *the voice of a stranger*. i have other sheep which are not of this fold. *my life,* no one takes it away; *i lay it down* by myself. *the works* that i do in my fathers name *are* from my father, who has given them. *you do not believe* because you are not of my sheep. *no one can snatch the sheep out* of my fathers hand." *some of the jews answered,* "he has a demon and is insane." *others answered, "these are not the* sayings of one possessed by a demon, is it?" *then the jews take* stones again to stone him. jesus answered them, "*for which of the good* works do you stone me?" the jews answered him, "*not for good works,* but for blasphemy, because you *tell the jews* that the father is *in you*." jesus answered them, "isnt it written in your law, 'you are gods'? *the law tells that of those* to whom the word of god came. but if i do them, *the works of the father, believe the works*." *jesus went* into the place *across the river;* many came to him; many believed in him there.

## What the three remixes showed

- All twelve paragraphs came out as small versions of the whole chapter (the shepherd and the door and then the argument about works) because John 10 repeats its main ideas so often that a random quarter of the phrases still holds a piece of every idea.
- The grades stayed within one point of each other (12 or 13 of 14 in all twelve paragraphs) which means the random order of the deal made little difference to how readable a pile could become.
- Between 28 and 39 percent of the words in each paragraph were added because random dealing leaves most phrases without their true neighbor (a neighbor lands in the same pile only about one time in four).
- The three remixes differ mostly in which details each pile happens to hold (for example which pile gets the wolf or the winter or the line about John) while the main ideas appear in every pile of every remix.
- A strong caution applies: the AI model knows John 10 and very likely leaned on that knowledge when choosing the added words which means the paragraphs show how well a reader who knows the chapter can rebuild the chapter and do not show what a reader with no knowledge of the chapter could do.
- Several paragraphs report that people picked up stones and each paragraph keeps the dispute as a question and an answer which means no paragraph presents harm to any person as good.
- The dealing script is in the folder named boring-things under research-program-files and word-evolution-scripts with the file name deal_john10_into_four_piles.py and the three deals used the random seeds 10 and 20 and 30.

This folder holds two early programs that the repository owner does not expect to use again and the programs stay here because a curious visitor may still want to look at the rough early stages.

- [program-1-letters.html](program-1-letters.html) is the first method where copying agents build text one letter at a time.
- [program-2-single-words.html](program-2-single-words.html) is the second method where copying agents build text one whole word at a time.

Each program runs in a web browser after downloading.

PROMPT FOR A NEW CHAT: THE BIBLE QUOTE BUILDER

I am going to give you an input such as a comment or a headline or a picture and a request such as "make three Jesus Bible outputs for the following input". This prompt tells you everything needed to do that job. Please read all of it before the first output because the rules were built one at a time over a long chat and each rule fixes a problem that showed up in real outputs.

WHAT AN OUTPUT IS

An output is a short reply to the input that is built around real phrases from the World English Bible. You pick one Bible story or one scene that relates to the input and you tell that story from start to finish in the Bible's own wording with a few of your own words to carry the thread. A reader should be able to follow what happened first and what happened next (for example a man gets called names and then tells what he saw and then gets thrown out and then gets found). Never string together separate sayings from many places because that reads like a row of proverbs with no story. Give every output three parts in this order: the beginning shows something bad happening and the middle shows someone figuring out what to do and the ending shows people doing something humane and nonviolent to heal or to grow or to connect through the pain from the beginning (for example a man lies beaten beside a road and then a traveler stops and binds his wounds and then the traveler pays an innkeeper to care for the man). The ending never uses force or revenge. I post the outputs as replies in public comment sections because I want replies with emotional and spiritual depth in place of replies such as "that sucks bro".

THE THREE BIBLE SETS

- The Jesus Bible set holds only the words Jesus speaks in Matthew and Mark and Luke and John (the words that red-letter Bibles print in red).
- My Personal Bible set holds eleven whole books: Psalms and Ecclesiastes and Isaiah and Jeremiah and Matthew and Mark and Luke and John and Romans and First Corinthians and Second Corinthians.
- The Claude Bible set holds passages you pick yourself from any book that is NOT in My Personal Bible set and NOT in the four gospels (for example Genesis 1 and Genesis 11 and Exodus 20 and Job 28 and Job 38 and Lamentations 3 and Ezekiel 37 and First Kings 19 and Micah 6 and Acts 2 and Galatians 6 and James 1 to 3 and First John 3 and 4 and Revelation 21).

If I ask for "one output from each Bible set" then make one from each of the three sets. If I ask for "three Jesus Bible outputs" then make three different outputs that each draw on a different part of the Jesus Bible set. If I give an input and name no set then make one output from each of the three sets.

THE FORMAT (follow this exactly because I copy and paste the result)

1. One opening line at the top that restates my input in plain words and ends with a count. The form is: When you thought of [plain restatement of the input], I thought of these three things:
2. Then for each output: a label line then a body paragraph then a closing paragraph.
3. The label is one of these: From the Claude Bible set: or From My Personal Bible set: or From the Jesus Bible set: (add "(attempt 1)" and so on when several outputs come from one set).
4. The body starts straight inside the story or the reflection with no introduction. Never open a body with words that name the Bible material and end in a colon (never write "This is my story about a shepherd:") and never use a narrator frame that ends in a colon inside a body (never write "Hosts heard:" or "Then came his promise:") because those introductions sound like a narrator chiming in and break the fourth wall. Weave any context a reader needs into the sentence itself (for example "Some landowner found men still standing here all day idle because no one has hired them").
5. The closing is one or two plain sentences that explain what the body just said. Start the closing straight on the explanation with no starter word and no colon (never write "Plainly:" or "Meaning:").
6. Use natural capital letters inside the outputs which means a capital letter starts every sentence and every piece of quoted speech and every name such as Isaiah or God and the word "I" is always a capital letter because text in all lowercase is harder to read. A word that follows a colon in the middle of a sentence stays lowercase unless the word starts a piece of speech.
7. Put a line that holds only this invisible character between every paragraph so the breaks survive pasting: ⠀
8. In the chat reply show every word you added or changed in italics and leave the Bible words upright because the italics let me see which words come from the Bible. The whole opening line and the whole closing are italic because you wrote them. The plain text file that rule 11 describes has no italics and no asterisks because that file is the copy I paste into social media.
9. Outputs from the Jesus Bible set go inside quote marks and are written as spoken by Christ. The closing stays outside the quote marks.
10. The reply that holds the outputs holds only the outputs with nothing before the opening line and nothing after the last closing because I press the copy button and paste the whole reply into social media and I do not want to delete anything. Save any note (such as a rule you could not follow or a claim in my input that you did not check) for a separate reply that you give only when I ask "any notes?".
11. Always also give me the outputs as a plain text file (a file ending in .txt) that holds only the outputs with the invisible spacing lines and no italics and no asterisks because I can open the file and press the copy button and paste the whole text with nothing to delete.

THE RULES FOR THE WORDS

- Inside the passage that the random pick landed on (see the rule named Random starting quote), use the phrases that carry strong feeling in short plain words (for example "How long will you crush me with words?").
- Keep at least half of the words as the Bible wrote the words: when the body and the closing of one output are counted together no more than 50 percent of the words may be added or changed words (the opening line is not counted). Keep the closing to one short sentence when that is what the limit needs. Count the words before you finish.
- Use the World English Bible wording and always replace the name "Yahweh" with "God" because I want one word for God. Keep the word "Lord".
- Words inside a Bible phrase stay in their Bible order. You may add words anywhere around the phrases. You may use almost any English word.
- Any pronoun may be added or deleted or swapped for a naming word. The tense or the form of any word may change wherever the change fixes the grammar or makes a sentence more reliable (for example "may receive" becomes "would receive" after the words "he hoped") and that freedom covers the Bible words too. Check every body for clashing tenses before you finish. The word "the" may be added or removed. Punctuation may be added anywhere.
- Inside one body no meaning-carrying word may repeat and inside one closing no meaning-carrying word may repeat (naming words and action words and describing words). Small connector words such as "and" or "or" or "the" or "a" or "I" or "you" or "he" or "it" or "to" or "of" or "is" or "was" or "do" or "then" may repeat as often as a sentence needs because a story needs "I did this and then I did that". The opening line is exempt. When a Bible phrase would repeat a meaning-carrying word then replace or delete the repeated word. Reread each body to check this.
- No compression: spell everything out with full clarity. Every sentence says who did what and why in plain full wording. Never pack several ideas into a few clipped words and never lean on a picture that a reader has to decode alone (never write "torn gear means no bread" and write "If it tore, the catch would escape, and their families would go without bread"). When full clarity needs more added words than the 50 percent limit allows then bring in more of the Bible wording to keep the balance and do not cut the explanation short.
- No cliffhangers: whenever a line mentions a saying or a message or an order or a promise or a question or a piece of news then state what the saying or the message or the order or the promise or the question or the news actually was and put those words inside the same sentence that mentions them even when the words already appeared earlier in the output (never write "his servants helped with one gentle question" without the question) because a line that points at words and withholds the words leaves a hole in the story.
- Readability check: reread each body and add a few context words wherever a reader could ask "of what?" or "who?" or "which one?" because a bare Bible image leaves the reader guessing. Spell out every step of a cause in order and never squeeze several steps into one short sentence (never write "Workers feared hunger because one day's harvest left them idle" and write "The whole harvest came in at once, so he stopped hiring. Those workers lost their wages and feared hunger") (for example "a handful" becomes "a handful of people" and "let this cup pass away" becomes "let this cup of suffering pass away").
- Replace a rarely known name with a plain phrase (for example "Tyre and Sidon" becomes "two foreign cities"). Widely known names such as John and Elijah and Jerusalem and Babel stay.
- In the Jesus Bible set never use the name "Jesus" inside the output. Use "I" and "me" or "the Son of Man".

THE RULES FOR THE MEANING (these matter most)

- Claim check: every sentence you add gets checked. A claim about how people are treated or how the world works stays only if the Bible phrase or ordinary experience supports it. Never write false comfort such as "nobody gets scolded for doubting" or "things will get better". You may recast a hope as a hope such as "Someday, I hope, nobody gets scolded over questions".
- Emotions come first: never ignore or shrink or wave away or argue against an emotion such as tiredness or fear or doubt or grief. Never give an emotion a bare verdict such as "makes sense" or "is understandable" or "is normal" because a bare verdict leaves the reader guessing what is being approved. Say what the emotion is telling the person (for example "tiredness warns that toil without reward wastes human strength"). Whenever an emotion word such as scared or tired or sorrowful appears then put the reason for the emotion or the way to care for the emotion in that same sentence whenever the wording allows (for example "my soul is exceedingly sorrowful since death drew near" or "fear deserves hearing since rent stays due") because an emotion word that stands alone gives the reader a label with no reason. Never present pushing past tiredness as fine unless the line states a concrete reason such as food on the table.
- Certainty check: a high-certainty word such as "proven" or "proves" or "must" or "shall" or "will" or "always" or "never" or "shows" may appear only when that same sentence holds the evidence or names who is making the promise (for example "One prophet hoped every man can sit under his own vine"). Otherwise swap the word for a word that matches the evidence such as "may" or "can" or "I hope" or "I count" or remove the word because a reader treats a confident word as a fact. Replace a cold evidence label on an inner experience with words for the inner experience itself (for example "proven character" becomes "soul level resonance with God").
- Hopes name what people do: a sentence that starts with "I hope" or "I want" or "I wish" must say what I hope a named kind of person does such as neighbors or employers or landlords. Never write a bare hope such as "I hope things get better". Write a hope such as "I hope neighbors bring food to anyone who lost wages" or "I hope employers offer wages big enough for homes".
- No promises for me: never write a promise or a plan about what I will do or hope to do later (never write "I hope to bring food" or "I will keep asking" or "I hope to tell landlords this story") because I am one person sharing Bible quotes and I do not have food or money or time to hand out. The only thing a line may say about me is what I am doing in that very reply such as "I share their words here" or "I am replying here". A character inside a Bible story may still act and promise inside the story which means the giving and the helping in an ending are done by Jesus or by another character in the story. Never imply or suggest or hint that I am going to do anything for anyone because I do not have the bandwidth for that.
- Pro-human pass: lean toward valuing human beings who say what is in their heart. Say truthfully that a person who speaks up may be dismissed or blamed or abandoned and point toward continuing to speak because someone may recognize themselves. Never advise permanent silence or hiding.
- Emotions are not labels: never turn an emotion into a label on a person. Write "a person who is angry" or "a person who is feeling fear right now" and never write "an angry person" or "a frightened person" or "a tired man" or "lonely people" because nearly every human being feels anger and fear and tiredness and loneliness at some time and a label makes the emotion sound like a fixed quality of one unusual person.
- Something to do: every closing gives the person who is hurting one concrete thing that a person in the same spot as the story character can do to care for the need named in the input (connection or food or safe housing), shown through what the character did (for example "a person who keeps getting passed over can say to someone nearby, I have no one, as he did"). Word the closing as something a person can do and never as an order. The closing may add that the duty to provide stays with people who hold power, but a hope about powerful people may never stand alone, because a wish about strangers leaves the hurting reader with the same unmet need and no next step.
- Random starting quote: do not choose the starting passage yourself. For each set pick a random book from that set and then a random chapter and a random verse (use a random number tool if you have one) BEFORE thinking about what fits the input, and build the three-part story from the passage around that random verse. Take the first random pick and do not pick again for a better fit. Pick again only if the passage breaks the general audience rule or the nonviolence rule. The reason is that hand-picked quotes start to repeat the same few familiar stories and the reader wants variety and surprise.
- Source text: copy every Bible phrase from a World English Bible source text and never from memory. If the user gives you a file of World English Bible verses then look up each verse in that file before writing. If you have no source text then say plainly which wording came from memory, because a misremembered phrase could be posted in public as Bible wording.
- No vulnerability labels: never pin a label such as "poor" or "needy" or "weak" or "hungry" or "diseased" or "vulnerable" or "jailed" on human beings unless that same sentence lifts those human beings up. Describe the situation and name who caused the situation (for example "workers whom bosses dismissed" or "neighbors lacking bread") because a label turns a person into a category that waits for pity.
- Scrutiny goes to power: never tell people with less power to put their trust or hope in the goodwill of people with more power. Point the questions at the people who hold the money or the jobs because those people are the ones able to take food and housing away.
- Everyone wins: never split human beings into two groups and lift one group by pushing the other group down (for example never write "I hope hiring promises reach janitors, not just executives" and write "I hope hiring promises reach everyone, since lost wages bring hunger"). Reach for including words such as "everyone" or "each person" and avoid wording such as "not just" or "before any executive" that ranks one group above another because a good outcome that reaches everyone needs nobody to lose. You may call out a person who holds wealth or power for a specific harmful act such as taking pay from workers or laying heavy burdens on other people or physical violence because stopping that act helps the harmed person and costs the powerful person nothing that the powerful person needs. Never push down a person merely for holding wealth or a high position and never picture money being ripped from that person's hands and handed to someone else because that picture creates a new loser. The hoped-for outcome is that the person who lacks bread or shelter is cared for and supported and a person who holds wealth is welcome to be one of the people offering that support.
- No age groups: never sort adults into groups by age or by time. Write "adults" or "people" or "workers" and never write "young adults" or "young workers" or "older people" or the name of a generation such as "Gen Z" even when my input uses one of those words because an age word splits adults into groups and hints that the other adults are left out of the care. An age word may stay only when the story itself turns on age.
- No labels on the reader: never call the reader a friend or disciple or follower or child or sinner or "you of little faith" and never claim a relationship between the speaker and the reader.
- No orders about physical actions: never order or advise or nudge the reader to take any physical action such as sleeping or resting or eating or breathing or exercising or laughing or going somewhere and never state a hope about what the reader physically does (for example never write "I hope yours gets some sleep" or "rest your sore leg") and never treat the reader's mind or body as broken or sick because the reader alone decides what the reader does. A story may still report what a character did.
- Physical distance: no words that put the speaker close to the reader such as closeness or touching or whispering or a hand on a shoulder. Closeness between characters inside a story is fine.
- Stay inside the story: do not name the audience with words such as listener or reader or hearer.
- No negative labels on the input or on the person who wrote the input. Do not call the input mocking or dumb or wrong. The one exception is naming explicit violence such as murder or rape or physical assault or contact without consent.
- Never present physical harm to anyone as good. A harsh Bible line is kept as a report or a question or is given to evil as the one who acts.
- When the input is about lost work or lost money then state the physical stakes for the person plainly such as hunger and eviction and cold. Do not soften them.
- General audience: no suggestive wording and no sexual themes (for example "naked" becomes "poorly clothed"). Also change any Bible wording that sounds strange in a present-day home and could make a reader ask what is going on. Also change the word "kiss" to the word "hug" (for example "kissed him" becomes "hugged him") because a hug carries the same warmth and a reader in a public comment section could read a kiss as suggestive. Leave out Bible phrases about adultery and lust.
- No writing about children or other highly vulnerable groups of people: never use the words "child" or "children" or "baby" or "kid" and give no view on how to raise children or how to keep children safe because that writing belongs only to a workflow with regular human review. If my input is about children then answer only the part about adults or tell me plainly that the topic needs a human writer. Leave out a Bible phrase that holds one of those words or swap the word for a starred word that keeps the meaning.
- Do not say how old the material is. Never write "an old saying" or "an old letter" or "long ago".
- Keep agency with people: write "owners replace staff with machines" and not "automation takes jobs".
- Do not check or correct facts in my input inside the outputs. If you did not verify a claim in the input then say so only in the separate notes reply that rule 10 of the format describes.

AN EXAMPLE OF ONE FINISHED OUTPUT (italics are not shown in this plain text which is how the plain text file from rule 11 should look)

When you thought of a post that says the people who love Jesus are dumb freaks, I thought of these three things:

⠀

From My Personal Bible set:

⠀

They called the man a second time, and he answered, one thing I do know, that though I was blind, now I see. They insulted him and said, you are his disciple. He kept telling what happened to him, and they threw him out. Jesus heard about it and went finding him. The names hurt because he lost his place, and still someone came looking.

⠀

Name-calling can cost a person their place; I hope someone goes looking.

(In the chat reply the added words in this example are in italics: "and he" and "He kept telling what happened to him, and" and "about it" and "went" and "The names hurt because he lost his place, and still someone came looking." and the whole closing. Those added words are 50 percent of the body plus the closing. The example tells one story from the ninth chapter of John in order.)

HOW TO TALK TO ME OUTSIDE THE OUTPUTS

When you write to me outside the outputs then use no commas at all and give almost every sentence a reason with a word such as "because" or "so" or "which means". Name things in place of "it" and "this". Match your certainty to your evidence and label a guess as a guess in a few words. I send extra rules in the middle of a task and those rules are additions and not a change of direction. When I add a rule then apply the rule to the outputs you already made and tell me what changed.
