# The current rules of the Bible quote builder

This page lists every rule that is in force for the Bible quote builder as of 11 November 2026 so that another person or another AI model can repeat the method.
The Bible quote builder is a working name for an experiment where short phrases from the World English Bible are shuffled by a program and an AI model (Claude) then connects the phrases into a readable passage under rules that the repository owner set one at a time.
Each rule below comes with the reason the repository owner gave or the reason the rule turned out to matter because a rule with no reason is hard for another person to apply well.

Warning about changed wording: passages made under these rules are not exact Bible quotes because the rules allow added words and changed pronouns and replaced names and replaced repeated words which means a reader who wants the exact wording needs to open the World English Bible itself.

## The source text and the three selections

- The text is the World English Bible because that translation is free for anyone to copy.
- The Claude selection is 35 passages picked by the AI model from books outside My Personal Bible set and outside the four gospels (for example Genesis 1 and the tower of Babel in Genesis 11 and Job 28 and First John 4) and the selection holds no passage from First Corinthians or Second Corinthians from 11 November 2026 onward because the repository owner added those two books to My Personal Bible set.
- My Personal Bible set (called the personal selection on the older pages) is eleven whole books which are Psalms and Ecclesiastes and Isaiah and Jeremiah and Matthew and Mark and Luke and John and Romans and First Corinthians and Second Corinthians (the repository owner removed Proverbs and added the two letters to the Corinthians on 11 November 2026).
- The words of Jesus selection is the words that red-letter Bibles print in red in Matthew and Mark and Luke and John.
- A program cuts the text into key phrases of about four words at punctuation marks and before linking words such as "and" and "for" because a phrase of that size usually makes some sense alone.

## How the phrases get shuffled

- Method A (copying agents): ten agents copy and paste key phrases and a simple reader favors strings whose neighboring phrases are also neighbors in the Bible which rebuilds true stretches of the text in a shuffled order.
- Method B (dealing): the phrases of one chapter are dealt at random into four piles and each pile is turned into one paragraph using every phrase in the pile.
- Method C (random set in random order): a program draws 8 or 16 phrases at random from a selection and shuffles the set and the AI model must keep that exact order because a fixed random order tests whether joining alone can make sense of unrelated phrases.

## Rules for connecting the phrases

1. Stars mark every added or changed word because a reader needs to see which words came from the Bible and which words came from the AI model.
2. In method A and method B the stretches may be placed in any order because a free order lets every sentence pair a claim with a reason and in method C the drawn order must be kept.
3. Words inside a phrase stay in their Bible order because the phrase is the unit the experiment is testing.
4. Joining words may be added anywhere (for example "and" and "because" and "so" and "but" and "while" and "those" and "here") because the cutting removed the links between thoughts.
5. A naming word that already appears in the passage may be reused anywhere because that reuse says who or what a sentence is about without bringing in an outside subject.
6. Each selection has special words that may be added anywhere which are about 12 of its most used naming words and action words and describing words (for the words of Jesus the list starts with father and man and son and god and kingdom) because an action word lets a gap hold a whole small claim.
7. The name "yahweh" is always replaced by the word "god" because the repository owner wants one word for God and keeps the word "lord" because "lord" connects with Christ for the repository owner.
8. Any pronoun may be added or deleted or swapped for another pronoun or for a naming word anywhere because a passage full of "he" and "him" and "they" leaves a reader guessing who is meant.
9. A word may change its form when a swap would break the grammar (for example "i have told" becomes "jesus has told") because a correct sentence is easier to follow.
10. The word "the" may be added or removed anywhere because the cutting often leaves a phrase with a missing or doubled "the".
11. Periods and commas and question marks and quote marks may be added anywhere because the cutting removed every mark and quote marks show who is speaking.
12. A rarely used name is replaced with a generic phrase that makes sense (for example "tyre and sidon" became "two foreign cities") because a reader who has not studied the Bible will not know the name and widely known names such as John and Jerusalem stay.
13. Passages from the words of Jesus are read as spoken by Christ which means the added words avoid the name "jesus" and use "i" or "the son of man" because the speaker in the gospels rarely uses that name for himself.
14. As few words as possible repeat inside one passage as long as the readability grade stays high because the repository owner wants every word to be different.
15. Almost any English word may be added and a repeated word inside a phrase may be replaced or deleted when the unique word rule would otherwise hurt readability because the short special list forced clipped wording.

16. When the repository owner gives an input quote such as a headline the AI model may add or delete or change any word so that the passage reads as a plausible answer or reflection on that quote as long as the change raises readability or relevance because the repository owner wants the builder to respond to a topic and not only to shuffle text.

17. When the repository owner gives an input quote the passage opens with one sentence in the form "when you thought of ... i thought of ..." and the sentence has no length limit and must give full context which means the first half restates in plain words the part of the input quote being answered and the second half says which Bible material the passage draws on because a reader who has not seen the input quote needs to know what is being answered.
18. The opening sentence is exempt from the unique word rule and carries no stars because the AI model writes the whole sentence and a clear sentence needs to repeat small words.

19. After the remixed passage the AI model adds a second paragraph of one or two sentences that explains in plain words what the passage just said and the explanation may reuse words from the passage or the input quote and no word may repeat inside the explanation because a reader gets the point fastest from a short plain summary.

20. Every sentence that the AI model adds is checked for claims about how people get treated or how the world works and a claim stays only when the source phrase supports the claim or when ordinary experience supports the claim because a comforting line that is false (for example "nobody gets scolded over unbelief") tells a reader who was argued with or shunned or abandoned for not sharing a belief that the treatment never happened and a claim that fails the check is reworded to match the source or removed or recast as a stated hope in the voice of the speaker (for example "i want a world where nobody gets scolded over unbelief" or "someday i believe nobody will get scolded over unbelief") because a hope tells a reader what the speaker wishes for and makes no false statement about how people are treated today.

21. Before every output the AI model makes one more pass over the word choices with a lean toward valuing human beings who put their heart and soul into words and the pass says truthfully that a person who speaks up may be dehumanized or told a real experience did not happen or abandoned and the pass points toward continuing to speak because some listener may recognize themselves in the words and the pass removes or rewords any added line that advises permanent silence or hiding because that kind of line can push a reader who is already alone to stop reaching out.

22. Before every output the AI model checks that no line puts a label on the reader that the reader did not choose (for example "friend" or "disciple" or "follower" or "lover" or "you of little faith") and that no line claims a relationship between the speaker and the reader because a stranger who is told "you are my friend" or "you are my disciple" has had a bond declared without consent and is likely to stop reading and a line that fails the check is reworded so that it describes an action or an offer and leaves the choice with the reader.

23. No line may describe physical closeness between the speaker and the reader (for example "closeness" or touching or a hand on a shoulder or whispering in an ear or any act that only happens when two people stand right next to each other) because a reader who meets that wording from a stranger pictures an uninvited person in their space and the wording is fine when the closeness happens between characters inside the story.
24. Passages avoid stepping outside the story to name the audience (for example "listener" or "reader" or "hearer") because the passages are meant to be little stories and a line that points at the audience breaks the story and the opening form "when you thought of ... i thought of ..." stays because that form answers the input quote.
25. Every word that the AI model added or changed is shown in italics in every output and the whole opening sentence and the whole closing explanation are in italics because the AI model wrote both in full which means the words in plain upright type are the words that come from the Bible phrases and a reader can see at a glance how much of a passage is source and how much is addition. The repository owner added a companion rule on 11 November 2026: every chat reply with outputs also comes with a plain text file that holds only the outputs with spacing lines and no italics because copying an output from a chat reply pastes the italics markers as asterisk symbols and the plain text file gives the repository owner a clean copy to paste into social media.
26. No output puts a negative label on the input quote or on the person who wrote the input quote (for example "mocking" or "dumb" or "stupid") because a negative label judges the person before the reply has said anything and gives the person a reason to stop reading and the one exception is naming explicit violence such as murder or rape or physical assault or contact without consent because naming violence plainly is how violence gets called out.
27. When one input quote gets several outputs the restatement of the input appears once at the top in the form "when you thought of ... i thought of these three things:" and each output underneath is a short paragraph that starts with a few words naming its Bible material because repeating the same long restatement inside every paragraph made each paragraph about half restatement.
28. Each output carries a label that says which set of Bible text the output came from and the three labels are "From the Claude Bible set" and "From My Personal Bible set" and "From the Jesus Bible set" and the middle label says "My Personal" with capital letters so that the words read as a label and uses those words in place of a name because any person who picks their own books can call that set their own which means the label fits whoever posts the output.
29. Every output stays suitable for a general audience which means no suggestive wording (for example the word "naked" beside people is replaced with wording such as "poorly clothed") and no sexual themes because the outputs get posted in public comment sections where readers of any age may see them and a source phrase that carries such wording is reworded or left out. The repository owner added on 11 November 2026 that this rule also covers Bible wording that sounds strange in a present-day home and could make a reader ask what is going on because a line that fits a one-room house of Bible times can pull a general reader out of the story. The repository owner added on 12 November 2026 that the word "kiss" is replaced with the word "hug" (for example "kissed him" becomes "hugged him") because a hug carries the same warmth and a reader in a public comment section could read a kiss as suggestive.
30. No output describes how old its material is or when the material was written (for example "an old saying" or "an old letter" or "old writers" or "long ago") because the age of a line adds nothing a reader needs and the repeated word "old" makes the outputs sound stiff and words about age stay only where age is part of the story itself such as old wine beside new wine.
31. This rule was replaced by rule 40 on 11 November 2026. The replaced rule asked every body to open with context words such as "this is a preacher asking" and the repository owner removed those openings because the openings read like a narrator stepping in front of the story.
32. Every body gets a readability check before the body is finished which means the AI model rereads each phrase and adds a few context words wherever a reader could ask "of what?" or "who?" or "which one?" (for example "a handful" becomes "a handful of people" and "let this cup pass away" becomes "let this cup of suffering pass away") because a bare Bible image leaves the reader guessing what the image stands for and a few added words lock the meaning in so that the rest of the sentence becomes easier to read. Every step of a cause is spelled out in order and several steps are never squeezed into one short sentence (for example "Workers feared hunger because one day's harvest left them idle" became "The whole harvest came in at once, so he stopped hiring. Those workers lost their wages and feared hunger") because a reader who has to rebuild the missing steps alone stops and asks what the sentence means. If this rule is skipped then the only result is that a reader may misread the line or give up on the paragraph.
33. Emotions come first in every output which means no line may ignore or shrink or wave away or argue against an emotion such as tiredness or fear or doubt or grief and no line may give an emotion a bare verdict such as "makes sense" or "is understandable" or "is normal" or "follows naturally" without saying what the emotion is telling the person (for example "tiredness without reward makes sense" becomes "tiredness warns that toil without reward wastes human strength") because a bare verdict leaves the reader guessing what is being approved and the reader may even hear approval for working past tiredness with nothing gained. Whenever an emotion word such as scared or tired or sorrowful or joyless appears in an output then that same sentence also says what the emotion points toward (the reason for the emotion) or how to care for the emotion whenever the wording allows (for example "my soul is exceedingly sorrowful" becomes "my soul is exceedingly sorrowful since death drew near" and "fear deserves hearing" becomes "fear deserves hearing since rent stays due") because an emotion word that stands alone gives the reader a label with no reason and the reason is the part that lets a reader recognize their own situation. No line may present pushing past tiredness as fine unless the line states a concrete reason that the person would accept such as food on the table. If this rule is skipped then a reader who is worn out may hear that the tiredness does not count and may keep spending strength on work that returns nothing.
34. Every output uses natural capital letters which means a capital letter starts every sentence and every piece of quoted speech and every name such as Isaiah or God and the word "I" is always a capital letter because text written in all lowercase letters is harder to read and a reader cannot see quickly where one sentence ends and the next sentence begins. This rule replaces the earlier habit of writing every output in lowercase letters. If this rule is skipped then the only result is that a reader may find the reply harder to read and scroll past.
35. No line may order or advise or nudge the reader to take any physical action such as sleeping or resting or eating or breathing or exercising or laughing or going somewhere and no line may state a hope about what the reader physically does (for example "I hope yours gets some sleep" and "rest your sore leg" are both removed) and no line may treat the reader's mind or body as broken or sick because the reader alone decides what the reader does and a stranger who hands out instructions about sleeping or eating sounds like a boss or a doctor that nobody asked for. A story inside an output may still report what a character did (for example "exhausted, he spoke; bread arrived, rest followed") because a report about a character gives no order to the reader. If this rule is skipped then a reader may feel managed or diagnosed by a stranger and may stop reading or stop sharing what is in the reader's heart.
36. A high-certainty word such as "proven" or "proves" or "must" or "shall" or "will" or "always" or "never" or "shows" may appear only when that same sentence holds the evidence or names who is making the promise (for example "One prophet hoped: Every man will sit under his own vine" keeps the word "will" because the sentence says a prophet hoped so) and otherwise the AI model swaps the word for a word that matches the evidence such as "may" or "can" or "I hope" or "I count" or removes the word (for example "size never proves worth" became "I do not count size as worth") because a reader treats a confident word as a fact and may repeat a guess or a wish as if somebody had tested the claim. A cold evidence label on an inner experience is replaced by words for the inner experience itself (for example "perseverance builds proven character" became "perseverance growing into soul level resonance with God") because the reward of long effort is felt inside a person and a word such as "proven" makes the reward sound like a certificate handed out by a judge. If this rule is skipped then a reader may trust a claim that nobody checked and may make a real decision on top of that claim.
37. The tense or the form of any word may be changed wherever the change fixes the grammar or makes a sentence more reliable (for example "may receive" becomes "would receive" after the words "he hoped" and "nobody gave" becomes "nobody gives" beside the word "tells") and this freedom covers the words that come from the Bible phrases too because a Bible phrase lifted out of its own sentence often carries a tense that clashes with the new sentence around the phrase and a clash in tense makes a reader stop and reread. Every body gets a grammar check for tense before the body is finished. If this rule is skipped then the only result is that a reader may stumble on a sentence and lose the meaning.
38. No output pins a vulnerability label such as "poor" or "needy" or "weak" or "hungry" or "diseased" or "vulnerable" or "jailed" on human beings unless that same sentence lifts those human beings up (for example "parts which seem to be weaker are necessary") and the AI model describes the situation and names who caused the situation in place of the label (for example "poor people" becomes "workers whom bosses dismissed" and "hungry people" becomes "neighbors lacking bread") because a label turns a person into a category that waits for pity and hides the people whose choices produced the hunger or the lost job. No sentence may tell people with less power to put their trust or their hope in the goodwill of people with more power and every sentence about a gap in power points the questions at the people who hold the power (for example "ask poor people, because rich neighbors might return the favor" became "skip rich neighbors, who might also return that favor. So gifts traded among wealthy circles deserve questions") because the people who hold money or jobs are the people able to take food and housing away and those people are the ones whose choices deserve a close look. If this rule is skipped then a reader who is short on money may feel described as a helpless type and may hear that the only way forward is to wait for a wealthy person to be kind.
39. No output splits human beings into two groups and lifts one group by pushing the other group down (for example "I hope hiring promises reach janitors, not just executives" became "I hope hiring promises reach everyone, since lost wages bring hunger") which means the AI model reaches for including words such as "everyone" or "each person" wherever an including word fits and avoids wording such as "not just" or "before any executive" or "more than princes" that ranks one group of people above another group because a line that takes from one group to give to another group disconnects people and leaves somebody out and a good outcome that reaches everyone needs nobody to lose. Rule 38 still asks that questions go to the choices of people who hold power and this rule adds that the questions stay on the choices (such as a choice to dismiss workers) and that the hoped-for outcome includes every person on both sides of the choice. The repository owner spelled out the line between a fair call-out and a split on 11 November 2026: an output may call out a person who holds wealth or power for a specific harmful act such as taking pay from workers or laying heavy burdens on other people or physical violence because stopping that act leaves the harmed person better off and costs the powerful person nothing that the powerful person needs which makes stopping the act a win for both sides. An output may never push down a person merely for holding wealth or a high position and may never picture money being ripped out of that person's hands and handed to someone else because that picture creates a new loser and repeats the harm in the other direction. The hoped-for outcome is that the person who lacks bread or shelter is cared for and supported by the people around that person and a person who holds wealth is welcome to be one of the people offering that support. If this rule is skipped then a reader on either side of the split may feel pushed out and the reply may feed a fight between groups where a shared good was possible.
40. No body opens with an introduction that names the Bible material and ends in a colon and no closing opens with a starter word and a colon such as "Plainly:" or "Meaning:" and no sentence inside a body uses a narrator frame that ends in a colon such as "Hosts heard:" or "Then came his promise:" which means every body starts straight inside the story or the reflection and any context a reader needs is woven into the sentence itself (for example "Some landowner found men still standing here all day idle because no one has hired them") because an introduction with a colon sounds like a narrator chiming in again and again and that breaks the fourth wall and pulls a reader out of a reply that is meant to feel personal and reflective. The single opening line at the top of a reply ("When you thought of … I thought of these three things:") stays because that line speaks to the person who wrote the input. If this rule is skipped then the only result is that a reader may feel talked at by a narrator and stop reading.
41. The AI model picks the Bible phrases for each output by hand from inside the named Bible set and chooses phrases that carry strong feeling in short plain words (for example "How long will you crush me with words?") because a test on 11 November 2026 found that hand-picked phrases read about one school grade easier than phrases that came from a shuffle. No more than half of the words in one output may be added or changed words which means that when the body and the closing are counted together the words in italics are at most 50 percent and the words that stay as the Bible wrote the words are at least 50 percent (the single opening line at the top of a reply is not counted) because an output that is mostly added words stops being a Bible remix and becomes the AI model talking with a few Bible words sprinkled in. The repository owner set this limit on 11 November 2026 and the outputs made before that date have not been rewritten to meet the limit. If this rule is skipped then a reader hears mostly the AI model and little of the Bible wording that gives the reply its weight. The hand-picking part of this rule was replaced by rule 52 on 12 November 2026 and the 50 percent limit stays in force.
42. Small connector words may repeat as often as a sentence needs which means words such as "and" or "or" or "the" or "a" or "I" or "you" or "he" or "it" or "to" or "of" or "is" or "was" or "do" or "then" do not count against the rule that no word repeats inside one body or one closing and that rule now covers only the words that carry meaning such as naming words and action words and describing words because a ban on repeating "I" or "and" makes a story impossible to tell (a storyteller cannot say "I did this and then I did that") and the outputs turned into a row of separate sayings with no thread. Each output tells one Bible story or one scene from start to finish so that a reader can follow what happened first and what happened next and each added sentence continues that same story (for example an output follows a man who gets called names and then tells what he saw and then gets thrown out and then gets found) because a reader stays with a story and drifts away from a list of proverbs. The repository owner set this rule on 11 November 2026 and the outputs made before that date have not been rewritten into single stories. If this rule is skipped then an output reads like several messages spoken at once and a reader cannot feel a story carried through the paragraph.
43. Every hope line names what people do which means a sentence that starts with "I hope" or "I want" or "I wish" says what the speaker hopes a named kind of person does (for example "I hope things get better" is banned and "I hope neighbors bring food to anyone who lost wages" is allowed and "I hope employers offer wages big enough for homes" is allowed) because a hope with no action is a person staring into the distance and a hope that names who could do what gives the hurting person something real to picture. Rule 48 limits what a hope line may say about the speaker.
44. Human beings rank first in every output which means any human being ranks above food and rent and money and no line may place a human being beneath those things. No output may tell or nudge people to limit what people do with their own lives because each person alone decides what that person does with that person's own mind and body. When food or shelter is missing then the output says that the duty to provide food and shelter sits with the surroundings which means the people who set wages and rents and the community around the family (for example "whoever sets prices and wages owes families enough") because rent and food are needed for human life and still rank beneath the human life that the rent and the food are for. The repository owner set this rule on 11 November 2026 because a line that praises people for going without until the rent is covered speaks on behalf of the people who made the rent too high and turns a shortage that those people created into a duty on everyone else. The first wording of this rule held examples about family life and those examples were removed on 12 November 2026 under rule 54. If this rule is skipped then a reader hears that the reader is the problem and the people who set the rents and wages hear nothing asked of them.
45. No output sorts adults into groups by age or by time which means an output says "adults" or "people" or "workers" and never says "young adults" or "young workers" or "older people" or the name of a generation such as "Gen Z" even when the input uses one of those words (for example "many young workers earn rent only" became "many workers earn rent only") because an age word adds nothing to the meaning of the sentence and splits adults into groups and hints that the adults outside the named group are left out of the care. Every adult receives the care in the output. An age word may stay only when the story itself turns on age (for example "a man waited thirty-eight years"). If this rule is skipped then a reader outside the named age group may feel that the reply is not for that reader.
46. Every output is a small story with three parts in this order. The beginning shows something bad happening such as a traveler with no room at an inn or a ruler loading people with burdens. The middle shows someone figuring out what to do such as a traveler making a bed in a stable or a person asking whether life is more than food. The ending shows people doing something humane and nonviolent to heal or to grow or to connect through the pain that the beginning described such as neighbors arriving or a story being carried to other people or a person asking those who hold bread to share bread. The repository owner set this rule on 11 November 2026 because a reply that only names pain leaves a reader in the dark and a reply that jumps straight to comfort skips the pain and the three parts together carry a reader from the hurt through the thinking to an action that a person can take. The ending never uses force or revenge and never asks anyone to be harmed. If this rule is skipped then an output reads like a complaint with no way forward or like comfort with no pain behind the comfort.
47. No output leaves a cliffhanger which means that whenever a line mentions a saying or a message or an order or a promise or a question or a piece of news then the output states what the saying or the message or the order or the promise or the question or the news actually was and states those words inside the same sentence that mentions them even when the words already appeared earlier in the output (for example "his servants helped with one gentle question" became "his servants said, if the prophet had asked you to do some great thing, wouldnt you have done it?") because a line that points at words and then withholds the words teases the reader and leaves the reader with a hole in the story. When the withheld content is an act of violence then the output names the act plainly as a report and keeps the person who gave the order as the one who acts. If this rule is skipped then a reader is left guessing what was said and may fill the hole with a wrong guess.
48. No output makes a promise or a plan on behalf of the speaker which means no line says what the speaker will do or hopes to do later (for example "I hope to bring food to anyone who lost wages" and "I will keep asking builders" and "I hope to tell landlords this story" are all banned) because the speaker is the repository owner and the repository owner is one person sharing Bible quotes who does not have food or money or time to hand out and a promise that the repository owner did not make and cannot keep is a false statement about a real person. The only thing a line may say about the speaker is what the speaker is doing in that very reply such as "I share their words here" or "I am replying here". Every other hope names what some other named kind of person could do such as neighbors or employers or landlords. A character inside a Bible story may still act and promise inside the story which means the giving and the helping in an ending are done by Jesus or by another character in the story (for example "Then I went to those holding the storehouse and requested loaves" inside the Jesus Bible set). No line may imply or suggest or hint that the repository owner is going to do anything for anyone because the repository owner said on 11 November 2026 that he does not have the bandwidth for that. If this rule is skipped then a reader may hold the repository owner to a promise that the repository owner never made and a hurting reader may wait for help that is not coming.
49. No output compresses its meaning which means every sentence spells out who did what and why in plain full wording and no sentence packs several ideas into a few clipped words or leans on a picture that the reader has to decode alone (for example "torn gear means no bread" became "If it tore, the catch would escape, and their families would go without bread" and "a flood of results can break one net or fill every boat" became "The catch was too big for one boat, so the crew called partners") because a compressed line saves a few words and costs the reader the meaning and a reader who cannot tell what is going on stops reading. When full clarity needs more added words than the limit of 50 percent allows then the AI model brings in more of the Bible wording to keep the balance and does not cut the explanation short. If this rule is skipped then a reader has to guess what a clipped line means and may guess wrong or give up.
50. No output turns an emotion into a label on a person which means an output says "a person who is angry" or "a person who is feeling fear right now" and never says "an angry person" or "a frightened person" or "a tired man" or "lonely people" (for example "I hope people near an angry person ask something similar" became "I hope people near a person who is angry ask something similar") because anger and fear and tiredness and loneliness are emotions that nearly every human being feels at some time and an emotion is either active in a person at this moment or not active and a label such as "an angry person" makes the emotion sound like a fixed quality of one unusual person as if that person had caught something that other people do not have. The wording that puts the person first and the passing emotion second lets the output treat the person as a whole human being who is feeling something right now and who deserves care while the feeling lasts. If this rule is skipped then a reader who is feeling anger or fear may feel marked as a type and set apart from other people.

51. Every closing gives the person who is hurting one concrete thing that a person in the same spot as the story character can do to care for the need named in the input (such as the need for connection or food or safe housing) and the closing shows that action through what the character did (for example "a person who keeps getting passed over can say to someone nearby, I have no one, as he did"). The closing is worded as something a person can do and never as an order because nothing bad follows for a reader who does something else. The closing may also say that the duty to provide stays with the people who hold power (such as people who hire) but a hope about powerful people may never stand alone. The repository owner added this rule on 12 November 2026 because a line such as "I hope people who hire meet each applicant in person" wishes the problem away and leaves the hurting reader with nothing to do for the need tonight. Without this rule a reader who is suffering gets sympathy plus a wish about strangers and walks away with the same unmet need and no next step.

52. The starting quote for each output is chosen at random by a program and never chosen by the AI model which means the program picks one random phrase from the Jesus Bible set and one random phrase from My Personal Bible set and one random chapter from the Claude Bible set and the AI model then builds the three-part story from the passage that surrounds each random pick. The AI model takes the first random pick and does not pick again to get a better fit and the only reason to pick again is a passage that breaks the general audience rule or the nonviolence rule. The repository owner added this rule on 12 November 2026 because hand-picked quotes had started to repeat the same few stories (such as the vineyard workers and the friend at midnight) and the repository owner wants variety and wants to be surprised sometimes. Without this rule the AI model keeps reaching for the same familiar passages and readers who see several replies start to see the same stories over and over.

53. Every Bible phrase in an output is copied from the verses file in the folder named bible-source and never from the memory of the AI model which means the AI model looks up each verse in that file before writing and the random picker draws from the modified copy named bible-verses-for-outputs.txt which leaves out the genealogies and the long lists of names because a row of names gives almost nothing to build a reply from. The repository owner added this rule on 12 November 2026 when the repository owner supplied the full World English Bible because the AI model had already misremembered one gospel line and the wording for the Claude Bible set had never been checked against a source. Without this rule a misremembered phrase could be posted in public as Bible wording and a reader could repeat the wrong wording as scripture.

54. No output written by the AI model talks about children or about any other highly vulnerable group of people which means no output uses the words "child" or "children" or "baby" or "kid" and no output gives any view on how to raise children or how to keep children safe (for example an exchange about a father and a baby daughter became an exchange about a rival holding out an open hand and "a child who laughed" became "a passerby who laughed") because children are highly vulnerable persons and a mistake in writing about children can lead to a real child being hurt and an AI model working alone has no person checking for that mistake. The repository owner holds that writing about highly vulnerable groups of people belongs only to a workflow with regular human review and oversight. When an input is about children then the AI model answers only the part of the input that is about adults or says plainly that the topic needs a human writer. A Bible phrase that holds one of those words is left out or the word is swapped for a starred word that keeps the meaning (for example "Wisdom is justified by her children" became "Wisdom is justified by her results"). Rule 44 still ranks every human being above money and from 12 November 2026 onward an output states rule 44 with words such as "families" or "human beings" in place of the words for children. The repository owner set this rule on 12 November 2026 and on the same day the examples about children were taken out of the older rules on this page and out of the corrections page and out of the record pages because an old line that sits in public can still be read as advice even when a fix sits beside the old line. If this rule is skipped then a reader may act on unchecked writing about a child and a child who cannot speak up may be the person who pays for the mistake.

## The reasoning behind rules 20 to 24 spelled out

The repository owner asked the AI model to spell out the logic of the five newest rules and this section records that reading so another person can judge whether the logic holds.

- One idea runs under all five rules: a passage read as spoken by a figure with great authority lands on a stranger who never asked for the passage so every added word has to respect the stranger as a person who decides for themselves.
- Rule 20 (check added claims) follows from that idea because a smooth sentence in an authoritative voice gets believed and a false comfort such as "nobody gets scolded over unbelief" tells a person who was shunned that the shunning never happened.
- Rule 21 (lean toward human expression) fills the gap that rule 20 leaves because removing false comfort alone could leave a bleak passage and the lean gives a true kind of encouragement which is that speaking may be met with dismissal and is still worth continuing because some person may recognize themselves.
- Rule 22 (no labels on the reader) follows because a label such as "friend" or "disciple" declares a bond that only two people can agree to and a declared bond from a stranger reads as presumption and can also read as a claim on the reader.
- Rule 23 (keep physical distance) is the physical version of rule 22 because a word such as "closeness" or "whisper" places the speaker inside the space of the reader without an invitation.
- Rule 24 (stay inside the story) follows because a story lets a reader step in at their own pace while a line aimed at "the listener" singles the reader out and turns a story into an instruction.
- Rules 20 and 21 pull against each other in a useful way because rule 21 wants encouragement and rule 20 only allows encouragement that ordinary experience supports which is why the passages say "may" and "might" about how others will respond.
- One tension remains open: the opening form "when you thought of ... i thought of ..." speaks straight to a "you" which sits close to what rule 24 avoids and the form stays because it answers a quote the person actually wrote and makes no claim about who that person is.
- A second tension remains open: an encouraging line such as "keep speaking your heart" is phrased as a direction and a reader could hear a direction from an authoritative voice as pressure so wording such as "speaking your heart stays worth doing" would leave more of the choice with the reader.

## Rules about harm and about honesty that always apply

- No passage may present physical harm to any person as good and a line about harm from the source is kept as a report or a question or is given to evil as the one who acts.
- Every choice about who a pronoun points at and every outside word is an interpretation by the AI model and the results pages say so.
- Each passage is graded against seven sentence rules from the page named writing-rules in the folder named writing-rules with a top score of 14 and the AI model grades its own passages which means every grade is a rough guide.

## What the rules do taken together

- The early rules (1 to 5) keep nearly all meaning in the Bible phrases and gave grades of 6 to 12.
- The middle rules (6 to 13) gave grades of 12 to 14 and moved a large share of the meaning to the AI model.
- The last two rules (14 and 15) make every word different and gave grades of 12 to 13 on random phrases in a random order while 37 to 49 percent of the words came from the AI model.
- The page named bible-quote-builder-how-the-outputs-evolved in this folder shows a sample output from each stage and the page named full-record in this folder holds every passage in the order the rules were added.

## Outputs under the first fifteen rules

Claude selection (12 of 14 with 58 different words out of 58 words) from the eight phrases in this drawn order: "before you" and "that he" and "whoever shall put away his wife" and "if only you god" and "ask of the father" and "for they think" and "than these is of the evil one" and "dont sound a trumpet":

- *mercy walks* before *every traveler, so* that he *who stumbles finds welcome.* whoever shall put away his wife *must first weigh her sorrow.* if only you, god, *would soften hard hearts!* ask of *your* father *plainly,* for *proud people* think *louder prayers win; anything showier* than these *quiet words* is *from* the evil one. dont sound a trumpet.

personal selection (12 of 14 with 48 different words out of 48 words) from the eight phrases in this drawn order: "they were exceedingly astonished" and "who are these" and "whatever you will ask" and "from a far country yes" and "and a spirit of justice to him" and "his disciples asked him about the parable" and "for justice but behold oppression" and "for those":

- *villagers* were exceedingly astonished: "who are these *strangers?*" "whatever you will ask," *came one reply* from a far country, "yes, and *true* spirit of justice to *any judge.*" his disciples asked him about the parable. "*people hoped* for *fairness,* but behold, oppression *arrived instead; stand alongside* those *crushed.*"

- "*visit your neighbor* and tell him, 'friend, *comfort comes at an hour* that you *cannot* expect; therefore dont be afraid.' *if dread speaks, reply,* 'get behind me, satan.' from one end of *earth people mourn,* sitting in sackcloth; *carry light with*in yourselves, *because whoever does so* doesnt stumble."

# Three Bible selections fed to the same word evolution experiment

This page compares what ten copying agents build when the agents draw words and quotes from three different selections of the World English Bible which is a modern English translation that anyone may copy freely.
An AI model (Claude) ran the test on 11 November 2026 and no other person has rerun the test yet which means every number here is a single unconfirmed analysis.

## How the experiment works

- Every quote is a piece of 3 words or more and at most 44 letters cut from the chosen text which means some quotes are parts of sentences.
- Ten separate agents each start from one random word and every paste copies a string with a chance of adding or swapping or changing one whole word and no deleting.
- The added words are drawn from the same selection and common words are drawn more often because the draw follows how often each word appears.
- A reader favors strings that hold more different complete quotes and a longer quote earns more credit and a half-finished quote earns partial credit.
- Earlier versions of the experiment changed one letter at a time and the letter version became too slow for large quote lists (about 100 to 500 pastes per second) while the word version ran about 600000 to 1000000 pastes per second on the same machine.

## The three selections

- Claude selection: 1837 quotes from 41 well-known passages of about 10000 words such as Genesis 1 and Psalm 23 and the Sermon on the Mount and the love chapter in First Corinthians.
- personal selection: 38236 quotes from ten whole books which are Psalms and Proverbs and Ecclesiastes and Isaiah and Jeremiah and Matthew and Mark and Luke and John and Romans.
- Words of Jesus: 6198 quotes cut only from the words that red-letter Bibles print in red (about 38500 words) in Matthew and Mark and Luke and John.
- An earlier run used thirteen books for the personal selection and included the words of Jesus from Acts and Revelation and the repository owner asked for Genesis and Galatians and Hebrews and those two extra sources to be removed.

## What the agents built after 2000 minutes of experiment time

Claude selection (about 10 quotes per agent):

- One agent: "i will deliver him / and you know me / and your father / before him all the / for i was hungry / with all your strength / when he saw him / heaven and in your sight / and love remain / and be thankful"
- Another agent: "and with all your might / and we are his / like a father has / and know my heart / and be exceedingly glad / yourselves on the earth / for i was hungry / for it is written / and be thankful / and he in god / out of heaven saying"

personal selection (about 13 quotes per agent):

- One agent: "and dont sin / you righteous people / that i may live / upward for the wise / things to your heart / and will have / and there they will be / with his brothers / so he will come / but those who were / all of the disciples / you wont believe / not to the flesh"
- Another agent: "he is yahweh / and all the righteous / the heart of the wise / should eat and drink / are in the earth / like the wilderness / and will rejoice / themselves in him / to the sword / take away therefore / and you shall have them / for the works which the"

Words of Jesus (about 11 quotes per agent):

- One agent: "when you pray / as in heaven / but sinners to repentance / word of the kingdom / but know this / and not perceive / given to god / and to return / distress in the land / but you dont believe / but because of the multitude / and you in me / of the synagogues"
- Another agent: "which of you / and to the nations / and the birds / and you shall have them / for from now on / resurrection of the righteous / and will tell him / the father himself / this is the will of / and are life / you know him / you will live also / and i in you"

## Differences that can be counted

- The most used content words for the words of Jesus were "father" and "life" and "believe" and "go" and "know" and "world".
- The most used content words for the personal selection were "disciples" and "yahweh" and "come" and "righteousness" and "father" and "righteous".
- The most used content words for the Claude selection were "earth" and "heaven" and "father" and "know" and "sight" and "love".
- The words "will" and "shall" made up 5 percent of the built quotes for the personal selection and 4 percent for the words of Jesus and 2 percent for the Claude selection.
- The words "you" and "your" made up 9 percent of the built quotes for the Claude selection and 8 percent for the words of Jesus and 6 percent for the personal selection.
- A warning about the "you" count: the share for the words of Jesus was 11 percent in the earlier run and 8 percent after two small sources were removed which means a gap of 3 points is within the run-to-run noise of this test.

## The same strings with connecting words added by hand

The AI model (Claude) took six of the strings above and added only connecting words such as "because" and "while" and "so" between the quotes and added no new nouns and no new action words which means every added word is marked with stars and every quote stays in the order the agents produced.
The added words are choices made by the AI model and are not part of the Bible text.

Claude selection:

- i will deliver him and you know me and your father *because* before him all the *while* for i was hungry *yet* with all your strength *then* when he saw him *in* heaven and in your sight and love remain and be thankful
- and with all your might and we are his *just* like a father has and know my heart and be exceedingly glad *among* yourselves on the earth for i was hungry *and* for it is written and be thankful and he in god *as if* out of heaven saying

personal selection:

- and dont sin you righteous people *so* that i may live upward for the wise *with* things to your heart and will have and there they will be with his brothers so he will come but those who were *with* all of the disciples *whom* you wont believe *but* not to the flesh
- he is yahweh and all the righteous *with* the heart of the wise should eat and drink *while* are in the earth like the wilderness and will rejoice themselves in him *until* to the sword take away therefore and you shall have them for the works which the

Words of Jesus:

- when you pray as in heaven but sinners to repentance *by the* word of the kingdom but know this and not perceive *whatever* given to god and to return *from* distress in the land but you dont believe but because of the multitude and you in me *out* of the synagogues
- which of you and to the nations and the birds and you shall have them for from now on *the* resurrection of the righteous and will tell him *that* the father himself *and* this is the will of *him* and are life *so if* you know him you will live also and i in you

What the connecting words changed:

- Connecting words made short stretches read like speech where two neighboring quotes happened to fit such as "so if you know him you will live also and i in you".
- Connecting words could not repair a quote that was cut in the middle of a sentence such as "for the works which the" because the missing part is a noun or an action word and the rule allowed no new nouns or action words.
- Each string needed only 4 to 6 added words because most quotes already begin with a connecting word such as "and" or "but" or "for".

## A second pass that also allows reference words already used in the string

The repository owner then widened the rule so that the AI model could add connecting words plus reference words such as "you" or "he" or "him" or "this" as long as the exact reference word already appears somewhere in the same string which means no new person or thing enters the string.

Claude selection:

- i will deliver him and you know me and your father *and i* before him all the *while* for i was hungry *yet you* with all your strength *then* when he saw him *from* heaven and in your sight *so you* and love remain and be thankful
- and with all your might and we are his *just* like a father has *his* and know my heart and be exceedingly glad *among* yourselves on the earth for i was hungry *and* for it is written *for yourselves* and be thankful and he in god *as if* out of heaven saying

personal selection:

- and dont sin you righteous people *so* that i may live upward for the wise *with* things to your heart and will have *those* and there they will be with his brothers so he will come but those who were *with* all of the disciples *whom* you wont believe *for they* not to the flesh
- he is yahweh and all the righteous *with* the heart of the wise should eat and drink *while you* are in the earth like the wilderness and will rejoice themselves in him *until he* to the sword take away therefore and you shall have them for the works which the

Words of Jesus:

- when you pray as in heaven but sinners to repentance *by the* word of the kingdom but know this and not perceive *this* given to god and to return *you from* distress in the land but you dont believe but because of the multitude and you in me *out* of the synagogues
- which of you and to the nations and the birds and you shall have them for from now on *the* resurrection of the righteous and will tell him *that* the father himself *and* this is the will of *him* and are life *so if* you know him you will live also and i in you

What the reference words changed:

- A reference word helped most where a quote was missing the one who acts such as "while you are in the earth like the wilderness" and "to return you from distress in the land".
- A reference word could not supply a missing action word which means stretches such as "until he to the sword" still lack the word that says what he does.
- The second string from the words of Jesus did not change because the first pass had already used the reference word "him" that appears in the string.

## Two more runs with new random starting points

The AI model reran all three selections twice more with different random starting points to see which differences repeat.

Claude selection in the second run:

- "god made the expanse / on the earth / your male servant / you his saints / know that yahweh / you are there / and know my heart / your father who is in heaven / your heavenly father / and you visited me / who is my neighbor"
- "in the beginning / fill the earth / which is on the surface / listen to me / made in the earth / he said to him / and in your sight / heaven and in your sight / and your father has / for god is love"

personal selection in the second run:

- "among the nations / by your name / for your loving kindness is good / and that which is / for all this / god is my salvation / and not spirit / no one answered / against all the / and there they will be / and against judah / which of you / into all the earth"
- "for who is god / because of your / therefore i love your / come with us / the neighbor and his / and not return / goodness of yahweh / and tell him / and it will be / he was troubled / as they went out / jesus came out / you from the father / righteousness through the"

Words of Jesus in the second run:

- "when you pray / he said to them / until you say / or in prison / and the last first / the lord is one / and i in him / for which of those / and go to the father / that you sent me"
- "judgment than for you / and not understand / that is to say / these will receive / and be killed / but when it is evil / and you will be blessed / and will tell him / why are you troubled / the hour comes / you dont believe me / for which of those / remain in me"

What repeated across all three runs:

- The word "earth" was the most used content word for the Claude selection in all three runs and "heaven" was in the top three in all three runs.
- The word "father" was the most used content word for the words of Jesus in all three runs and "know" or "believe" or "receive" appeared near the top each time.
- The words "yahweh" and "righteousness" appeared near the top for the personal selection in all three runs while the rest of the top words changed from run to run which fits a much larger and more varied source.
- The exact quotes changed almost completely from run to run which means a single run shows one draw out of many possible draws.

## A third pass on the second run that also allows a pronoun for any named person or thing

The repository owner widened the rule once more so that the AI model could add connecting words plus reference words already in the string plus a pronoun such as "he" or "they" or "it" that stands for a person or thing the string already names such as "god" or "the father" or "the earth" even when that pronoun appears nowhere in the string.
The AI model applied all three rules to the six strings of the second run and every added word is marked with stars.

Claude selection:

- god made the expanse on the earth *for* your male servant *and* you his saints know that yahweh *he and* you are there and know my heart *like* your father who is in heaven your heavenly father *for he* and you visited me *so* who is my neighbor
- in the beginning fill the earth which is on the surface *and* listen to me *about what he* made in the earth *as* he said to him and in your sight *from* heaven and in your sight and your father has *it* for god is love

personal selection:

- among the nations by your name for your loving kindness is good and that which is *yours* for all this *because* god is my salvation and not spirit *yet* no one answered *him* against all the and there they will be and against judah *so* which of you *with him* into all the earth
- for who is god because of your *and* therefore i love your *so* come with us the neighbor and his and not return *from the* goodness of yahweh and tell him and it will be *that* he was troubled as they went out *when* jesus came out *to* you from the father *with his* righteousness through the

Words of Jesus:

- when you pray he said to them until you say *it* or in prison and the last first *because* the lord is one and i in him for which of those *and they* and go to the father *so* that you sent me
- judgment than for you *if they* and not understand that is to say these will receive *it* and be killed but when it is evil and you will be blessed and will tell him why are you troubled *when* the hour comes *and* you dont believe me for which of those *who* remain in me

What the third rule changed:

- A pronoun for a named person let a quote lean on a name from an earlier quote such as "about what he made in the earth" where "he" points back to the one who speaks in "listen to me" and forward to "god".
- A pronoun for a named thing filled a gap after an action word such as "these will receive it" and "your father has it".
- The third rule still could not supply a missing action word or a missing thing word which means endings such as "righteousness through the" and "against all the" stay cut off.

## A fourth pass that allows any of the most generic words

The repository owner widened the rule a last time so that the AI model could add any of the most generic words such as "you" and "them" and "those" and "others" and pointing phrases such as "over there" and "here" even when no such word appears in the string.
The AI model read the rule as covering connecting words and reference words and pointing words and left out action words and thing words which means every added word still names nothing new.

Claude selection:

- god made the expanse on the earth *for you* your male servant *and for* you his saints *so* know that yahweh *and* you are there *with them* and know my heart *like* your father who is in heaven your heavenly father *for he* and you visited me *so* who is my neighbor *here*
- in the beginning *you* fill the earth which is on the surface *so* listen to me *about what he* made in the earth *as* he said to him *there* and in your sight *from* heaven and in your sight and your father has *it for them* for god is love

personal selection:

- among the nations *over there* by your name for your loving kindness is good and that which is *yours* for all this *because* god is my salvation and not spirit *yet* no one answered *him* against all the *others* and there they will be and against judah *so* which of you *with him* into all the earth
- for who is god because of your *own* and therefore i love your *own so* come with us the neighbor and his *own* and not return *from the* goodness of yahweh and tell him and it will be *that* he was troubled as they went out *when* jesus came out *to* you from the father *with his* righteousness through the *others*

Words of Jesus:

- when you pray he said to them *over there* until you say *it here* or in prison and the last first *because* the lord is one and i in him for which of those *over yonder* and go to the father *so* that you sent me
- judgment than for you *if they* and not understand that is to say these *here* will receive *it* and be killed but when it is evil *there* and you will be blessed and will tell him why are you troubled *when* the hour comes *and* you dont believe me for which of those *over there who* remain in me

What the fourth rule changed:

- Generic reference words closed the cut-off endings that the earlier rules could not close such as "against all the others" and "righteousness through the others" and "your own".
- Pointing words such as "over there" and "here" gave the strings a sense of a speaker standing in a place and pointing at people which the earlier passes lacked.
- The strings still lack action words in places such as "if they and not understand" because the rule still keeps new action words out.

## Limits

- The agents mostly built short common quotes because a short quote made of common words needs fewer lucky draws which means rare and famous lines seldom appear.
- The counts come from the best string of each of ten agents in one run per selection which is a small sample.
- A word such as "energy" for the feel of a text cannot be measured by this test and the counts above only describe which words appear.
- The reader counts quotes and has no sense of meaning which means the built strings are stacks of separate quotes and not flowing passages.

# Record of the chat behind the research pages

This page is a time-ordered record of one long chat between the repository owner and an AI chatbot (Claude) on 11 November 2026 which produced the research pages in this folder.
Each entry gives the request from the repository owner in his own words and then a short summary of what the chatbot did because the full replies of the chatbot run to many tens of thousands of words and would bury the requests.
The repository owner dictates by voice which means his requests read like speech and some words came out misspelled and the misspellings are kept as typed.
All times are United States Central time.

## The full chat word for word

The repository owner shared the whole chat as a public link and the link shows every word from both the repository owner and the chatbot up to the moment the repository owner made the link: https://claude.ai/share/a29d81cb-280d-4d44-a449-e84b9516b4f5
The repository owner refreshed the shared link on the evening of 11 November 2026 which means the same address now also shows the later part of the chat where the Bible quote builder rules and outputs were made and the pages named rules and best-outputs in this folder hold the results of that later part.

## Part 1: the Voynich manuscript

**11:32 The repository owner asked:** Can you please do research and attempt to solve or make progress on the voyniche manuscript if you can't directly solve the cryptography of the symbols maybe the images are looking to express something important from the author's point of view maybe you could do research on the author's upbringing or information about the author or the time period or someone in the location where the writing took place that kind of s*** I'm looking for if the cryptography is too impossible maybe you could get an idea of who wrote it or the village It Was Written in or the country It Was Written in and the time period it was written in all of those things could be progress towards figuring out what was the meaning behind that possible manuscript this is to take into account that all of the symbols could have been randomly generated on the person was just doodling and was totally not trying to send any message there could still be meaning there because a human being wrote it and that human being was born in a certain place and in a certain time period and may have been exposed to different historical events all of those things

What happened: the chatbot gathered the published evidence on the date (1404 to 1438) and the likely place (northern Italy) and the five scribes and the newest decoding attempts and said plainly that the chatbot could not read the text.

**11:34 The repository owner asked:** Okay now do novel research on the topic or someone has asked a question that has not received an answer and put a medium amount of effort into making progress or answering questions we're expanding Frameworks regarding the topic

What happened: the chatbot downloaded a public typed copy of the text and built a "next page" test that compares spelling habits at the bottom of one page with the top of another page.

**11:36 The repository owner asked:** Keep going

What happened: a ranking version of the test found that the writing continues from the first leaf of a folded sheet to the second leaf of the same folded sheet in one direction only and the chatbot corrected an earlier statement that had played the effect down.

**11:37 The repository owner asked:** Keep going go deep

What happened: the result held in three typed copies and 36 settings and a control showed the effect belongs to the single folded sheet.

**11:45 The repository owner asked:** All right keep going

What happened: an originality check found that other researchers had already reported the basic sheet resemblance and the chatbot counted 176 of 177 pages ending at a paragraph end.

**11:55 The repository owner asked:** All right now keep going

What happened: the chatbot could not open the journal article behind a visitor-screening page and found that sheets in the same bundle share word habits which suggests the binder kept piles together.

**12:01 The repository owner asked:** Now summarize all of your findings about this manuscript in a way that I can understand make sure to follow the principles of including because or similar words to explain whatever labels you are using within the same sentence every single time please this increases and improves readability and understandability for a general audience including me

What happened: the chatbot wrote a plain summary.

**12:04 and 12:05 the repository owner sent two sets of writing rules** which asked for sentences that stand alone and carry their own reasons and explain every label and avoid pronouns and commas and match confident wording to evidence.

What happened: the chatbot rewrote the summary twice under the rules and the rules themselves are in the page named writing-rules in this folder.

**12:16 The repository owner asked:** Okay great now can you do a top 10 bullet points from your findings for social media remember these are for social media people who might have limited emotional or mental bandwidth while scrolling

What happened: the chatbot wrote ten one-sentence findings.

## Part 2: hiding knowledge by splitting a book

**12:19 The repository owner asked:** So what if each four-page folded sheet uses a different Cipher because each one was by maybe a different author using a different form to hide the content Maybe like each author was given their own cipher to hide whatever they were told to write and the person telling them what to write did not want any of the ciphers to know what any of the other ciphers were writing

What happened: a word-count test argued against a separate cipher for every sheet and left a per-scribe difference open.

**12:23 The repository owner asked:** Like what if the manuscript was trying to hide some message that was incredibly important and the author may be only wanted and themselves and others to know and so had different scribes right out different portions that only when the portions are together does the full message of the manuscript actually makes sense do you see the logic I'm looking to describe like this logic of okay I have a book that needs all the parts to make something very dangerous like a nuclear weapon so then I separate the book like let's say in the four parts and separate all the parts and have scribes only right parts that when I read 1/4 of the book I cannot make a nuclear weapon so then I take those sheets which might look random but I give them to the Scribe and have them write it out in a cipher that only that scribe knows and then I have another scribe right part 2 of random pages that I put together to make sure if you only had part two it wouldn't make sense how to make a nuclear weapon and then have them encode that etc

What happened: the chatbot named the idea as secret splitting and listed what in the manuscript fits the idea and what pushes against the idea.

**12:24 The repository owner asked:** Now can you pontificate just on the logic of like let's say you had a book that had all of the steps needed to make a nuclear weapon using this process what would you be looking to do

What happened: the chatbot laid out six goals of a hider and the trade-off between the wrong person reading the book and nobody ever reading the book again and the reply covered only the logic of hiding.

**12:26 The repository owner asked:** Now can you rephrase it where it's like this energy of okay you have a book of like a thousand pages on how to make a nuclear weapon with extreme detail so then let's say you start randomly combining four different piles of pages you then read through the different piles of pages and you rank on a scale from 0 to 100 how much this would help you building nuclear weapon and you're trying to push the number close to zero as possible but your restriction is you must keep each individual page as it is you can't be flipping and flopping sentences it's only pages

What happened: the chatbot described the sorting moves that lower the score of the worst pile and why whole pages cannot reach zero.

**12:30 The repository owner asked:** Can you test this on like let's say you have a 1,000 page Biology book or something and then how much would it make sense like let's say you dealt them randomly and then you dealt them out in a specific way to maximize confusion somehow I'm not sure how that would work

What happened: the chatbot cut a public-domain biology book into 1000 pages and compared four ways of dealing and the results are in the page named hiding-a-book-by-splitting-pages.

**12:33 The repository owner asked:** What is the confusion Factor for each part where if you didn't even bother separating them how did you decide what is increasing confusion

What happened: the chatbot defined a confusion score from three kinds of lost connection and gave the score for every pile.

## Part 3: text that evolves by copying

**12:44 The repository owner asked:** Okay now can you run a test what would happen if you had some kind of word genetic algorithm where you are only allowed to copy and paste text and let's say you can do that up to 10 times a second and every time you paste there's a chance another letter will be added or a letter might shift or a letter changed but no deleting of letters this is so that the experiment is interesting could you construct sentences that make sense from the reader's point of view like some kind of natural selection where the users that are copying and pasting or trying to copy and paste things that make the most sense to them what would happen after several generations of this

What happened: with no reader the pool became gibberish and with a picky reader the pool froze on the word "in" and with a reward for more real words the pool slowly built a chain of common words.

**12:45 The repository owner asked:** And also are there any examples of this high secret secrecy tomb of knowledge that needs anyone but the most secure individuals to be able to know how to do it such as building nuclear weapons but also wanting to avoid any person working on improving the tome from knowing the whole tome to avoid Rogue actors learning how to make something devastating to others

What happened: the chatbot gave historical examples of split knowledge such as the atomic bomb program of the 1940s and the lost sea weapon of the Byzantine navy and the glassmakers of Venice.

**12:51 The repository owner asked:** And then now like the reverse tomb would be like let's say there's some very important goal like "a systematic way to increase love in the world towards others especially family and children" so how would you reverse the the book or whatever so that everyone can read it if the book was separated into a billion pieces of information scattered randomly amongst individuals you know what I mean

What happened: the chatbot reversed each hiding rule into a sharing rule such as pieces that are complete alone and many copies and pieces that point to neighbors and said the chatbot holds no proven contents for such a book.

**12:52 The repository owner asked** for the writing rules as text to paste into another chatbot and the chatbot returned the rules.

**12:55 The repository owner asked:** Can you rerun that genetic word experiment but have every single thing like everything that the reader sees add one letter like every second or something you can mess around with that this is to prevent local minimums like the word in there will be letters added to everything through Force every certain time period

What happened: forced letters broke the freeze and slow forcing (every 5 minutes) kept 90 percent real words while fast forcing (every second) left about 2 percent.

**13:02 The repository owner asked:** Can you make a program with different setting sliders that you can run this experiment and you can see the results happening before your eyes

**13:03 The repository owner added:** Can you also add to the program some kind of scoring where the sentence if it encodes a behavior that can be explained to another intelligent agent that gets a large bonus score so only commands like pick up the cup or love your neighbor those score pretty high compared to random strings of nouns or verbs

What happened: the chatbot built a live page with sliders and a bonus for command patterns.

**13:12 The repository owner asked:** Can you run some more experiments with this new setup that favors actionable statements

**13:14 The repository owner added:** Can you pontificate on the Reversed logic of the secret tomb to create like a tomb of something you want to share with the world like bring love to the world that kind of thing how that relates to the ministry of Christ how much was he following those rules or patterns you described

What happened: commands evolved only when partial steps earned credit and the chatbot compared the sharing rules with what the gospel accounts report about the teaching of Jesus without claiming to know what Jesus intended.

**13:22 The repository owner asked:** Can you maybe write out 10,000 common commands and the agent looks at the current string and the current string that is closest to the 10,000 common commands gets favored more to be copied and pasted the 10,000 common commands can be commands that make sense and maybe the agent would understand that is doing the copy and pasting let's say for example rerun the experiments

What happened: the pool reached an exact command such as "wash my dogs" within about 15 to 28 minutes of experiment time and forced letters hurt this fixed-target reader.

**13:45 The repository owner asked:** Can you have it where like if it's a long string a goal string might have the highest score if it has a copy of each command within it so the ideal command string would be let's say if it was 300 characters as many unique commands from the 10,000 command list as possible can you rerun the experiment knowing this

What happened: a first scoring rule stalled at one command and a corrected rule reached 7 to 13 commands per string.

**14:07 The repository owner asked:** And then maybe you could make a 10,000 command kind of story where the commands after they are settled upon by the picker the commands are then reordered at the end to be what the order would be from the original 10,000 command story thing this is to make the so-called random commands make more sense potentially from a narrative point of view instead of having like a series of commands that sounds nonsensical there's a chance they might sound more sensical if the original had the 10,000 commands in some kind of order and rerun the experiments

**14:08 The repository owner added:** And you could also consider commands that are closer together might have a higher score because that might signal the commands might make more sense because they are near each other in the 10,000 command story versus a random scattering of commands even if in the story order might not make much sense can you add that and rerun the experiments

What happened: sorting into the order of a one-day story cut the jumps between scenes by about half and the closeness bonus gathered commands into fewer scenes at the cost of fewer commands and more near-copies.

**14:50 The repository owner asked:** Can you add an additional bonus for the experiments of the number of unique words so repeated words like take my cup and take the cup and lift my cup is penalized because of the cup is used three times so there's a bonus for Unique words that can apply to every word so if the word the is used multiple times that's less of a bonus than unique words and rerun the experiments

What happened: the share of words that are not repeats rose from 64 percent to between 71 and 92 percent.

**15:53 The repository owner asked:** Can you make sure the program is updated with the latest rules for the genetic word thing and can you put a link into the chat for the artifact

**15:59 The repository owner asked:** For the other agents can you have them can you have like 10 agents all starting out with different random letters and see how they go I want to see like different outputs cuz right now it's like the same sentence repeated over and over in the bottom half of the app

What happened: the live program gained the latest rules and ten separate agents with private pools.
